text: Short version: Rude, incompetent, arrogant jerks. But what other choice do you have? Long version: My wife's 5-year old macbook was on the fritz. We took it in, they suspected a logic board/video problem and sent it off to a repair center (Apple Depot). It took a couple days longer than they said for the repair, but I suppose not the store's fault. My wife picked it up and paid the $400. It would have been a free repair if the problem had occurred 8 months earlier within the 4-year period when apple was covering the NVIDIA 8600M GT problem (see http://support.apple.com/kb/TS2377), but I digress. She noticed that somehow during the servicing by the Depot, the bottom panel got bent from the top in a way that is only possible when the machine is disassembled (or someone was super crafty with a knife/screwdriver). After the apple 'genius' confirmed it was not like this when she brought it in, they said they would get the part and "fix it right up". When the part finally came in, my wife made the half-hour trip to the apple store only to be told she'd need to leave it an additional 3-5 days. This was not an option at the time. I was not happy when I heard this story and how the 'geniuses' handled it. I got in touch with Gary the store manager to figure out how my wife could schedule a repair that wouldn't take 3-5 days given: 1) she'd been out of a computer for a week already 2) had never been told how long this add'l repair would take and, most importantly 3) the damage was Apple-caused. [update: 9/2013 - I neglected to note earlier that the depot (or the store) COMPLETELY WIPED HER HARD DRIVE CLEAN - which is utterly mind-boggling considering the entire chain of people had diagnosed the problem as the NVIDIA 8600M GT, not anything to do with software, the operating system, or anything associated with her hard drive. This created a major fucking headache for her (and me), but one Apple absolves themselves from any responsibility (up front) for doing, should it happen.] Gary tried to quickly undermine my concerns and absolve his store/Apple of responsibility stating that it would take at least two days to order the part to fix the Depot's damage anyway (though it was already ordered and in the store; he clearly couldn't be bothered to look at the details of the order) and that they were "brutally honest" about how long in-store repairs take. If "brutal honesty" is policy, then they should make sure everyone on staff knows it, because it's not being practiced by the 'geniuses'. Gary said he'd see what he could do and would call back. He talked to my wife when he called back, insisting how "unfair" it would be to put my wife ahead of others in line (which we never requested). All we wanted was a day and a time (tomorrow, next week, when-f*cking-ever!) and would given them a few hours to do a few hour job. Apparently, this is impossible for an Apple store's sophisticated workflow, regardless that apple caused the damage! Finally, Gary made the poor choice of adding a "secondary note" to the conversation; adding how my wife's computer had a chip (literally 2 mm long) on the corner (I guess he finally bothered to look into the details of her order), implying that she was responsible for the (completely unrelated) damage caused by the Apple Depot that his Apple store was so graciously going to do for free (over a 3-5 day window). Bad move, Gary.

text: That will be my one and only time at the Hotel Preston!! I stayed here last weekend and was very disappointed. The originally gave me a room that was right in front of the elevator....who wants to stay there? The front desk was helpful in getting me a new room but it didn't get much better. My floor was designated on as a non smoking floor but it sure didn't smell like it. Later that night I had to go down a floor to get ice and found the issue; the stair wells are used as smoking area and cigarette butts are everywhere!!! DISGUSTING!!! I even took pictures to send to the hotel. The hotel itself looks like someone took an old holiday inn and tried to renovate it into a trendy hotel but ran out of money. If you actually look at the quality of the hotel everything looks like it was just slapped together. The walls/doors are paper thin and you can hear everything. And what is going on with the elevator walls?!?! Looks to be a cow hide that was dyed red and had patches removed.... The rooms look fairly nice but the beds are uncomfortable and you are only full size beds in the rooms with two beds, for a 3.5 star hotel this just isn't okay. The bathroom sink area looks nice but the shower looks to have the original white tile that wasn't renovated with the rest of the hotel. Where is the fan in the bathrooms? I had to shower with the door open just so I could breath in there... The hotel offers a shuttle but beware its $18.00 to go downtown!! Its cheaper to drive yourself and park and much more convenient. We didn't figure this out until after we got in the van and were told by the other couple in there A 3.5 star hotel this is not!! text: We were supposed to stay at this hotel for two days this week for my husband's business trip. In fact, he was the speaker for one of the conference events in the hotel, so the room was to be complimentary for us. When we checked in, I was impressed by the look of the lobby, although the exterior of the hotel looks rather dated. After being given our room keys, we headed down a long hallway to our room, and I started to wonder if the carpet floors had recently been flooded because I thought I smelled water damage. The smell got worse the further we walked, and after hearing a few dogs bark from behind closed room doors and seeing signs such as "Do not open door. Chow inside", we realized that we were smelling dogs, and lots of them! Now, I adore dogs, but I do not like sleeping in rooms that smell like a kennel, so we walked back to the front desk to asked to be placed in a room that is not one in which animals are kept, nor near the barking ones. On the way back down the hall, I saw tufts of dog hair on the carpet, and my eyes were watering by the time we made it to the lobby. The front desk worker informed us that there were no rooms away from dogs, as 300 dogs were attending a "Chow Convention" in the hotel! I said I was amazed that they did not warn guests who might have allergies, and that I could not believe that there were not rooms that are set aside for people who do not want to stay where a dog has stayed. She said, "Well, we charge them a cleaning deposit". My response was, "A lot of good that does us right now." I next asked them to find us a room at a sister property, and she claimed that all king or queen-sized rooms were booked. So, we had to get on the Hilton site and find a room 10 miles away from this hotel where my husband had to work the next two days. I just went in to see him at the hotel conference room here, and they have done a good job of trying to mask the kennel smell by spraying disinfectant or room deodorizer everywhere, but you can still get a whiff of the tell-tale sign of dogs. Rest assured that if you stay in a room at this hotel, it is a room that a dog has stayed in, too.

text: You are not going to find a better tourist and local flavor shop than the Legends Gift shop. I am FROM here and I spent a good hour in here going through each aisle with my friends and literally laughing until we cried at some of the stuff available. Yes it is tacky. Yes they have some of the silliest stuff imaginable. - Marilyn Monroe and Elvis rubber toys for the bath - complete with ridiculous duck noses where their actual nose should be - Rock-n-roll magnets for your fridge. Plus any other kind of magnet - Elvis beanie babies. Why the hell did I want the red one so bad? I don't know, but I'm telling you I did. - drivers licenses with dead and living celebrities on them - What the hell is up with the coasters, magnets, and T shirts with the cartoon cats with the butt facing forward? Cat butts? Cat rear ends looking you right in the eye? What the FUUUUUCK!? We laughed until we cried at those. I have a cat in person and I don't want to see his butt in my face so why would I want that? Hilarious though!! Keep them in mind for your next white elephant exchange. - shot glasses, fake road signs, ashtrays, and the usual stuff you find in gift shops - these key chains that were made of sticky material in the shape of vajayjays that will stick to the wall. I won't even say what they were called but yeah, again, we laughed until everyone thought we were drunk - silly T shirts for all sexes and ages - Cowboy hats of varying coolness - Real guitars (although quality may not be good) - western belts and other type western wear In the front, across from the register area, they have a fortune telling machine with a talking Elvis. I. CANNOT. RESIST. ELVIS. Plus, he's dead so maybe he really can tell me my fortune. So I put the 50 cents in and he starts telling me how I basically need to talk less and listen more. Then he gives me a printout saying a similar thing but in a rhyming verse. It is like he KNOWS me or something! Not that I get wordy and talk too much. No way. Not me. Thank you, thank you very much Elvis. This place is just good clean fun for locals and tourists alike. Have an hour to kill downtown? text: A group of about 10-12 decided to try this place for happy hour. Several of the people in our party were smokers so we sat outside in the unseasonably warm weather. It was spitting rain, but there was a roofed gazebo we were sitting under so no worries. The smokers would go out of the gazebo to smoke as they were told this was the rule. The waitress was just, off, somehow. She wasn't very friendly and seemed overwhelmed and confused by simple requests like, "Can I see a menu?" About 30 minutes in, she came out and said the forecast was calling for storms and lightening and would we mind moving inside, but we didn't have to hurry, we could finish eating. Several of us had ordered food and about half of us were eating under the covered gazebo. We said, no problem, and continued on. About 10 minutes later as we were finishing up, she came out again and said she was getting off her shift and did we want to close out with her or transfer our tickets to another server? We all said we would close out so that she could get the tip money. She split our bill up, ran our cards and brought them back. During this time, she also delivered another food order to us outside. By this time, the sky is clearing and looking like the weather had passed by. Another 10 minutes go by and she says, "My manger is about to come out here and be really rude to you if you don't go inside." We responded by saying, "If that's his plan, then that's a really bad idea." She went back in and immediately the male manager/bartender came out and YELLED, "You have to come inside now, our insurance won't cover you being out here." He was incredibly rude. Since we had all just closed our original tabs anyway, we all left and went to another bar. I will never go back. The wings were overcooked and salty (the trainwreck style wings) and the service went from being sub-par to just flat out rude. There are a thousand different ways to handle this, the easiest would have been when that last food order was up, the waitress (or whoever our new server was going to be) could have said, "Would you like me to get a table set up for you guys inside for when your food comes out? " With a group of 10-12, a little assistance figuring out where to relocate would have made everyone's life a lot easier. Instead they lost a group of folks who are looking for a new happy hour venue, spend lots of $$, and drink all evening. To top it all off, most of us are former service industry folks. Dumb.

text: I'd like to preface this review by saying that of all the reviews I've given on Yelp, this is my first 1 star review. I am a pretty laid-back reviewer who does not fret about small details. The bad service and bad food my family had here, however, warrants this low rating. Honestly, Bertucci's or Olive Garden offer better Italian food than Spasso, and with better service. I've also heard great things about Trattoria Giuseppe on W Chester Pike. My family made a 5pm reservation for Christmas Eve to eat at Spasso for the first time. When we arrived, they sat us in a nice table in a large room to the side of the entrance. They then came over after a few minutes and told us they put us in the wrong place. Accidents happen, so that was fine. Our new table, however, was in the noisy foyer next to the entrance and the kitchen. It felt like we were sitting in a hallway. We saw many better tables open and were left to wonder why on Earth would they put us at what appeared to be the worst table in the restaurant. The manager then came over to us and began to interrogate us as if we never even had a reservation to begin with. She then emphasized in a condescending manner that the other table was not for us; it was for her friend. She eventually found our reservation on the sheet, but only after insulting us and making us feel unwelcome. Next the waitress came over to tell us about a special appetizer sampler with fried and grilled calamari, prosciutto, caprese, etc. We were a party of six, but we told her we only wanted the sampler for two. She seemed hesitant to do that, so my mom explained that, as 80% of the platter was seafood and meat, most of the group wouldn't be able to eat it, as two were vegetarians and two didn't eat seafood. She then had the nerve to say "Well, you're a party of six, so let's make it for 4?" Rude and inexcusable. What happened next solidified for us that the we would never come back to Spasso. One person ordered chicken parmesan while another ordered veal parmesan. When they brought out our food, we double-checked with the waitress to ensure that each person got the right one, as the person who ordered chicken parmesan does not eat veal and is disgusted by it. Unfortunately, even after we asked, the waitress mixed up the dishes, causing our one party member to feel sick after accidentally eating veal. When we told the waitress about her mix-up, all she said was "Oh, okay. Sorry about that. Does anyone want dessert?" in a completely apathetic tone. Terrible, terrible service. Now, to review the food. The veal parmesan, as other reviewers have said, is dry and flavorless. The chicken parmesan was also average at best, certainly not better than something you could get at Olive Garden for less money. I had the fettuccine pomodoro which was pretty good and only $13, perhaps the only item on the menu we ordered whose price matched its quality. The gnocchi gorgonzola tasted like candy, and not in a good way. The person who ordered it could not eat more than a few bites. My dad had the zuppa di pesce, which he said tasted like they just used a can of tomato paste to make the sauce. The plate cost $24, so there is really no excuse for the sauce to taste that bad. It would've tasted better if they had walked down to Trader Joe's and bought one of the jars of sauce they sell. Very disappointing to say the least. Media has tons of affordable, classy restaurants with great food. Spasso simply isn't worth a visit. The overpriced bad food, combined with the terrible, condescending service we received from the manager and the waitress, is going to keep any of us from ever eating at Spasso again.

text: Dined here on a Tuesday night with a group of 7 for a late dinner at 8:45pm. The ambiance before going to the restaurant was romantic - to say the least. The tree that was lit up with small lights, the crickets creating a melody with their little chirping, to the old trees with a lot class. However, I was surprised right away when we walked in. The restaurant is dressy; there are paintings of cats and dog everywhere including your plates; the chairs are huge as if from alice wonderland. The food was very good. If we were to base the restaurant on food alone, the restaurant would have gotten a 4 star. What did we have then? 1. Cheese Plate - Pick 4 different types of cheese for $20. A very good deal. We were able to share one cheese plate amongst 7 people. The cheese selection is varied and comes with a strawberry jelly, berries, bread & crackers. 2. Sides - Each side is able to serve family style. Mac and Brie - It's Mac and Cheese but creamier. The mac and brie was cooked perfectly - there was no run of extra cheese and there was a slight crunch from the top of the mac & brie. White Truffle Pomme Puree - I could not taste the white truffle in this dish and ended up just tasting like mashed potatoes to me. I would suggest not to order again. 3. Antelope - Yes, because it was antelope and I thought to myself, "When am I ever going to eat Antelope?!" The Antelope surprisingly was not too gamey nor chewy; it had a duck/steak- like consistency. The antelope was coated heavily with pepper which masked the true taste of the antelope. 4. Hudson Valley Duck Breast - I had a taste of the Duck Breast. This was one of the better dishes (compared to the Antelope and the scallops) as the chef maintained the flavor of the duck. The duck breast had a slighty crunchy skin but the juices flowed from the duck meat as you take a bite. The haricot vert on this dish was amazing and should have ordered it as a side. Overall, one of my coworkers described the dish as "a plethora of flavor". Each compenent of this dish had something to the table and was good even as standalone. What gave this restaurant 2 stars? Poor customer service. First, we were definitely a younger crowd in what appears to be an old - school spot for the locals. We felt like we were treated as such. There was no explanation of specials (if there were any) and no personal touch from the service. They carded us and looked suspiciously long on each id as if we were underage. Second, towards the end of the meal, yes it was getting late but NO need to close the lights on one of the side dining rooms on us. Once they turned that light off, the place was extremely dim and we felt we were being hurried out. Finally, we asked nicely about the smaller plates deal and they sternly told us that they could not accomodate us for a party of 7+ (yes a weird number to come up...not 6+ but 7+). We did have our hearts set out on the smaller plates deal but it didn't seem like they wanted to accommodate us or even suggest splitting into 2 tables.

text: Mixed reviews as noted by other reviewers. The service was AMAZING (that you pay for, of course!). The food we ordered received mixed reviews. I visited Indy with my wife for our first anniversary. We went to the Oceanaire Seafood Room for our formal dinner. I made the reservation online using opentable.com and noted to the maître d' that it would be our first anniversary. We were immediately greeted and congratulated upon entering and all of our waitstaff congratulated us without me saying anything. My wife was truly impressed! The service was impeccable. The meal begins with bread with butter (which would have been better if the bread was warmed). A dish of various chilled foods, including radishes, celery, carrot and peppers, was brought out as well. For our appetizer we shared the shrimp and grits, which was great! I thought the grits had a nice consistency and flavoring. The shrimp were slightly overdone for my taste. The dish lacked salt which I do not usually add, but in this case it improved the flavor considerably. (4/5) Our main courses were also mixed in quality. Presentation for everything was great. I ordered the Holland Sole stuffed with crabmeat for my entrée. The crab was sweet and delicious. The sole was baked and overdone. The meat was a little tough and dry. I have had sole before and remember it to be delicate and buttery in texture. My wife ordered the fresh sockeye salmon with portabella mushrooms and cherry tomatoes. The sockeye was grilled and had a better consistency and was cooked to perfection. (5/5) We paired our food with a side of steamed asparagus which was accompanied by a hollandaise sauce. The asparagus was crunchy and cooked well. The waiter recommended a sauvignon blanc, Wairau River for about $40 bucks. It was okay and my wife liked the light feel of the wine. I thought it was a little acidic, most likely aged in steel barrels. Overall, it went well with our meal. We shared the Burning Alaska dessert which was complimentary and a nice surprise! It's a thin layer of brownie topped with strawberry ice cream and marshmallow topping, on FIRE! In conclusion, I'd recommend the Oceanaire Seafood Room for special occasions and for those who appreciate impeccable service. The food was okay, but at these prices I'd expect more.

text: Before submitting this review, I briefly skimmed the notes of previous reviewers. Based on my experiences here, I'd agree on one thing: This place is a mixed bag. Before even entering the restaurant, I have to say that even the architectural design is confusing. What are there, like 3 floors?? Is this place THAT busy? What's up there? I've never been up there and no one seems to know what it's for. When I got to the front door, I noticed a valet booth and a couple of young men trading banter outside. This place has a valet?? Well, I don't want to get off on a rant too soon in this review so let me continue on. Inside, my friend and I stood for some time by the front entrance, waiting to be seated. I saw waiters and waitresses seemingly milling around but not really doing much at all. There was no hostess to be seen. After someone called from the back, a girl arrived to seat us. I think the exterior of this building is pretty sleek and maintains a modern flair, as does the interior. The ceiling has a very industrial feel to it with exposed pipes, air shafts and vents twisting over one another, headed this way and that. The furnishings themselves reminded me a hotel, though. I can't exactly explain why. The color scheme utilizes a lot of muddled down browns, blues and reds; very earthy tones. It was clean enough but I wasn't sure what vibe the owner was trying to create. When I reviewed the menu, I found the prices quite high for the offerings. Most of the dishes were what I would consider pretty classic Chinese dishes: chicken and vegetables, General Tsao's chicken, Kung Pao, Moo Goo Gai Pan, Mongolian Beef, etc. Typically, I find these dishes at a Chinese take-out joint for $6 to $7 . These dishes were all about $15. We were so hungry that we immediately placed an order. I put in an order for the Mongolian Beef at $14. There was no mention of a side of rice so I asked the waitress about rice. She stated that rice came with the order. Now, for some time, I waited for the order. I heard cooks in the background banging around, dishes crashing; the sounds of a furious food station cranking out delicious, hot, fresh meals. At the point that I was just about to ask the waitress where our food was, she arrived with the food tray and proceeded to hand us our dishes. She placed the Mongolian Beef platter before me and asked if that was all. I replied no, that the side of rice was missing. 5 minutes later, she returned and said it would be an extra charge. For rice?? In a Chinese restaurant?? Rice is like, one of the cheapest foods and typically, an Asian restaurant gives you rice whether you want it or not. For $15, I believe rice should be included. I explained this to the waitress and she left again. Later, she returned and said that while they do charge for rice, the chef allowed me a dish of rice this time. The waitress, again returned with a dish of fried rice. I took one bite of it and had to spit it out. It tasted like fiberglass! In addition, it was completely burned and dried out. After some time, the waitress came by to bring us the check and asked us how the food was. I explained that the rice was burned and dried. It absolutely felt like I was trying to eat glass. She mumbled something and went back to the food station, never to return again. Ok, let me sum up my thoughts. First of all, let's review the history of the joint. The restaurant is owned by Steve Ho, who was a former partner at 'Five Happiness' and had sold his shares in the restaurant shortly before Hurricane Katrina to open Hoshun. While Ho admits that the restaurant is a fusion of Chinese, Thai and Vietnamese cuisines, I'm confused as to what type of direction this restaurant was/is intended to go. The prices clearly suggest an upscale environment, as does the valet outside on the curb. To expound on this, why does the restaurant even have a valet?? Are they trying to attract wealthy customers? If that's the case, wealthy guests will know if it's truly a classy joint or not - and this place is NOT. While there are a few fusion dishes available on the menu, the presentation and flavor are average, at best. I didn't experience anything different here than I would in a hole-in-the-wall late night Chinese take-out. As a matter of fact, I've actually had BETTER Chinese food in some buffets. That's quite sad. To top it off, they tried to charge me for rice, which clearly should have come with the meal. If that wasn't enough, it was dried out, old and burned. Any restaurant, especially Asian, that cannot properly cook rice immediately gets a cross through their name in my book. In writing this review, I've not been able to locate a single accolade of the establishment since 2008, which is when they first opened, and I imagine that was ONLY because they were new. Hopefully, Hoshun can pull it together. New Orleans lacks a solid Chinese gourmet outside 'Five Happiness'

text: Took my nearly 4-year-old to a pre-hip hop/acro course. The class lasts for one hour and in the summer, you can just pay a $10 registration and then pay about $12 a class as you go (for summer, that's Tuesday and Thursday at 6:15). Although there were nine kids in the class, Jason was able to keep all the little people in their spots, spread out just so with the assistance of his class helper. He's quick, he keeps their attention, and he's been doing it for years (20-ish? I know a girl 32+ that had him when she was a KID--I guess dancing keeps you young because that man don't look like no grandpa!) He broke down various subjects--keeping a beat, learning some moves, flipping over wedges (focusing on muscles you would use for break dancing)...the songs were top 40 hip hop and the kids were diggin' it. Oh, and they broke out with the moon bounce at the end of class...just made a partition with one of the mats, and kept their little arms and legs moving while they blew that thing up right next to them. As I mentioned, there's one helper for nine kids...Jason said that the classes are much larger in the fall, but the number of helpers increases when the class size does. As to the business end of things, it seems organized (they take your information, you pay). The ATM next door was down (They take cash or check only), but the girl at the front was ok with me paying up at the next class. Although the 2-hour round trip on the train is a bit much, I think it's worth it. (For folks in the mainline burbs, trains only run every hour after around 6:50, so there's little time to get to suburban station via the local subway--I'll have to run my ass off to make it happen!) UPDATE (and also, perhaps, tooting my own horn here)...my commute from Oreland: Catch local train at 4:37 (catch the later one and will actually be late). Get to Market East around 25-30 minutes later. Take 15 minute bus down the street (time difference between taxi and bus--almost none bc of traffic lights). Be at least 30 minutes early for class (again, would otherwise be 10 minutes+ late. Grab coffee at gas station across the street. Maybe make friends gas station attendant so you can use this relationship for parking purposes in the future.). Dance class at 6:15. Dance class over at 7:15. RUN FOREST RUN for four blocks to subway after class--carry Omar while running bc of lights, misshapen roads, litter to trip over, etc. Take subway to Suburban Station. RUN BITCH RUN--little Omar also must run bc my back is out of commission at this point. Ask at least 10 people where regional rail is bc way is always different with construction...many may not know/care about your time constraints, but after several times asking,you will 90% of the time be pointed in the right direction, even if you run in a bit of a circle. (Note: print out map of Suburban Station.) Might make it 10 minutes early to airless underground sweat hole (If run like an Olympic competitor with tot in tow. RUN my small child, RUN, even though you just danced your ass off for one hour after a one-hour commute). Sweat. Soak Omar with wet paper towel. Hand sanitizer. Snack if time permits. (Must pack food/drinks as commute is long...really long and intense...you do not want french fries and other nasty greasy food on train. People will look at you as if you have no manners because eating smelly food on a public transit system is, indeed, very rude. Your starvation is not their business.) Finally, take 25ish minute regional train ride home. Give kid various toys to occupy him so he does not poke commuters in back of head or engage others in unwanted and intense peek-a-boo games (you see me bitch, now play!) Every Tuesday and Thursday.

text: Before I can really comment on the food itself, I must admit that I've had the pleasure of dining in Thailand multiple times. And although I have a culturally Thai background I expect more backing behind the title of "Bangkok Cuisine". My family and I went in for lunch and they have an awesome $8 combo plate served with a Curry Pop, White Rice, Fun See Pork Soup with the choice of 2 entrees dependent on the day. Couldn't go without ordering the Thai Iced Tea as well. YUMMO! The Fun See Pork Soup was very nice to see and reminded me of my childhood. It was garlicy, herby and hot but overly salted, so I added rice. (Just a note, I already like things pretty salty and am made fun of by my husband) When I ordered, I ordered in Thai and the hostess/waitress did not understand me...it made me kind of sad because I found out later that she is Korean. So, I ordered in English. The Chicken Green Curry with the Chicken Pad Thai seemed appetizing. I can say that the Pad Thai tasted like I had it in Thailand but did not have all the ingredients that it was supposed to contain. The sweet orange noodle dish is traditionally served with bean sprouts, crushed toasted peanuts, a wedge of lime, fried tofu, egg and your desired meat. Only the egg, a few pieces of chicken accompanied the noodles. Had to ask for the lime and the peanuts were in the condiment dishes to be added on one's own. Now the Green Curry is a large reason I give it 2 stars. I could see the separation of oil from the sauce and the sauce was filled with seeds from the bell peppers? I didn't know what it was from but I didn't like it. The sauce was so overbearingly salty. I ate a few pieces of the chicken and soggy bamboo shoots and let the rest of my dining experience become the yummy goodness of my Iced Tea. I later brought the rest of my food home and added about 2 cups more bamboo shoots, tofu, chicken and coconut milk to the leftover sauce and then it became perfect. Still salty but just the right amount. Overall, I wouldn't go back unless I was thirsty.

Again, the customer service was wonderful. The place is clean, and the prices are great. But even after asking for what I wanted several times, I still left with a less than desirable look on my hands and feet. text: I really hate to do this. Cochon's food is very good and I've enjoyed eating there a few times, but an experience last weekend has prompted me to give this low rating. We were entertaining out of town guests last weekend and went to Cochon for some post-parade dinner. The alligator appetizer was delicious and we were enjoying our drinks as well. We ordered the ham hock, which came to us covered in organic greens. I noticed that something was moving on the greens. A SMALL GREEN WORM WAS WIGGLING AROUND ON OUR FOOD! Now, I understand that they were busy that night (it is Mardi Gras, afterall) and no doubt the chefs were really churning it out., but this was so unappetizing and repellent that I pretty much lost my appetite. To top it off, we sat there for a full 10 minutes watching the thing squirm around our food before we were able to flag down a server. They were busy but when a waitress notices four people sitting at a table with a look of utter disgust on their faces, she needs to swing by and see what is up. We finally flagged down a waiter and he he swooped this off our table with a brief excuse about "You know, those organic greens". I realize this is a valid statement but c'mon, if I am served a bug on my food I need more of an apology from the waiter than a shrug. They brought out a new ham dish for us, which was good, but it was hard to eat after seeing such a disgusting image. I expected after that, that they would have comped the dish, sent out a free round of drinks or dessert or something to make amends, but when the bill arrived, they had charged us for the dish that had a worm., along with everything else. When a restaurant makes a mistake like this they NEED to make amends. Cochon is not cheap and it is not a little hole-in-the-wall taqueria. This is a finer dining establishment and in this case, I was not satisfied with their apology for serving me a writhing invertebrate. I have one other criticism: Last year, my business partner and I hosted a work dinner for about 12. When making the reservation, I told the hostess that this was an important work dinner and it would be nice if we had a good table for our party. They sat us right near the front door in Feb, which blasted freezing air every few minutes. We dropped about $800 at that dinner while our colleagues shivered through the whole meal. For a big important party like that, it would have been nice if they'd done more to accommodate us.

text: Walking in from the street, you might be pleasantly surprised what you find inside! I'm just glad Gerard Craft left provel off the menu! He gets a star for that. I'm slightly perplexed, this place is new to the scene and yet is featured in Esquire's list for Life Changing Pizza?! Are we serious here? This place is featured among the Ranks of Lou Malnati's in Chicago and Di Fara in Brooklyn. By no means am I saying that a St. Louis restaurant cannot make a list of this sort, but this seems a little off. Maybe that's just me.... As we waited nearly 35-40 minutes (we were told 90, so they delivered quickly), looking around it was busy. Servers and trainees floating in and out of the dining areas to the kitchen. Management offering table touches and guests standing around sipping wine and cocktails. The decor is simple and the overall feel is casual but slightly rustic. Tables covered in brown paper, medium body silverware with a dish towel style napkin greets diners. We started with with the fried rice ball dish, traditionally this is called Arancini. I am not certain why they didn't label this traditionally since other items on the menu are called by their Italian reference. The portion size is small, so order two if your a table of 6 or more. For risotto tossed in flour and fried, I think that they could be bigger or offer a few more per order, have a small and large order. The accompanying marinara had good flavor, but needed to be a little thicker. The aioli, seemed a little out of place for this dish. The rest of the food: - The Roman (Pizza) Look at my roman picture and look at others posted. Where's the bacon on mine?? It was lacking. I think each slice had about two small cubes of bacon. I would have expected more from this "life changing pizza". The crust was nice, airy slightly chewy and crispy where it needed to be. I'd eat it again! - Pappardelle, slow roasted pork with mascarpone and apples. This dish was on it's way to being good, but the noodles could have been spared about 2 more minutes to finish cooking. And there was something missing, it landed flat. Maybe it need a little sprinkle of something on top to give it that last extra push to greatness. - Oven roasted lasagna.Made with a bechamel, it was flavored nicely and had that hearty vegetable taste. What would have been a nice additive, had the server explained the vegetables inside. The menu reads "seasonal" should I anticipate that root veg will be in my lasagna and in the Spring I'll have something different? -Ending the meal: Gelato and Tiramisu, both were good. Assuming the tiramisu is made in house, I'd say it was very tasty and probably better than others I' have tried in St. Louis. The gelato was also good. We tried: pumpkin with bacon, telaggio with cherries and dark chocolate. Will I return? That's really what people want to know right? I return when I really, really enjoy a dish. When I see the art in the food I've had and I know that this is almost one of a kind, I go back for more. . Pastaria didn't really seal the deal for me. But since I know the other creations by Gerard Craft are on point, I feel compelled to revisit. :)

Also, on a special occasion like just before a major holiday, you may want to plan an amuse or two for guests. It could have moved you from a 4 star to 5. text: This is my update and one written on a more serious note than the last more fluff-filled review of admiring the decor and playing games on my phone: This place is terrible. So genius me some five years ago decided to pay the $75/year for a PO Box thinking that this would be the solution to all of my problems. Around the holidays you can forget it, trying to mail packages would get you nothing but huffs and puffs from the long line behind you and eye-rolls from the employees. After awhile I just felt uncomfortable buying anything other than stamps or sending something certified or with a return receipt...only the bare necessities. Was this really what I was paying for? My last apartment in Chinatown was a major upgrade from buildings I had been in previously. I actually had a doorman, I had package receipt service, I had my own mailbox...my days with USPS were over! NOT! I put a forward on my mail from the PO Box that I had to my new address and thought everything would be just great. My mail was delivered no problem, I had a great mailman, I occasionally left him little notes to let him know how much I appreciated his service. So now we fast forward a year... text: Don't get your panties in a wad before you get all up in arms about my one star rating. I have reason, and if you read on you will understand. First of all, I have to say that I was absolutely STOKED to eat at Saffron. I've heard a few friends rave about how delicious the food is and that I'm missing out by not eating it. I DISAGREE. Here's the breakdown, from the beginning: The online reservation system SUCKS. You input all of your info into the forms, requests date, time, and number of guest, etc. Then, the next page says "thanks for your reservation request. Not technically their fault, but definitely worth mentioning. STRIKE 2. So, when we finally arrive (10 minutes late even, due to traffic being ridiculous-Pacers game) we are greeted at the door by the chef's wife and immediately seated. At this point, I'm taking in the surroundings and loving the decor and the decadent aroma. MINUS ONE STRIKE. Our server, Shaq greets us, brings water, etc. Explains some of the "house specialties" since we are both first timers. The zaalouk was not flavorful at all and the bakoula tasted like an ashtray smells. Also, the cucumber and tomato that were served with the app seem to have been sliced at minimum two days ago. The Kafta Tajine was foul. Gorgeous, yet grotesque all at the same time. The "seasoned beef" resembles a dog turd (no, seriously), the peas tasted like they were fresh out of a freezer, and the entire dish was so salty I couldn't eat it. The bread that accompanied the dish was bland and dry. Lindsay's dish was decent. The salmon was cooked well, but the vegetables that came with it were raw in the center. Shaq seemed to forget about us. After he delivered our food, it was almost 40 minutes before he returned to our table. Of course I didn't want to take the leftovers home because it was gross. In addition, the chef's wife explained to me that the "reason" the tajine was so salty is because they have two new cooks training. STRIKE 25. All together, we will NOT be going back to Saffron. I don't have a clue why everyone on Yelp is in love with it. Everything about Saffron sucks.

text: After salivating for months over going to one of Chef Garces' restaurants we were finally able to visit Philadelphia and so we decided to go to Tinto, a Basque inspired pintxos place (tapas are called pintxos in the basque country) and we were not disappointed! We were promptly seated by a friendly hostess and our server Becky soon arrived with our menus. She was very attentive and helpful in answering all our questions about the menu. She explained the tapas conceptof the place and recommended quantities for us. We ordered a pitcher of Tinto sangria which was delicious, albeit a bit small, but surely enough to last through our whole meal (after all, this is not a college bar). The decor is very cool, resembling a wine cellar, with tons of bottles and corks on the wall behind the bar, but the highlight is the food, OMG!! We started with marinated 'boquerones' with pickled peppers and a drizzle of olive oil. The first thing my wife said was that it tasted like Bilbao, and after spending six months there, I think she knows what she's talking about. Next came the roast pork bocadillo, a small sandwich with pulled roast pork, quince jam and aged manchego, yuuuummmmmmmmmm, fingerlicking good!! We were still uuhhing and aahhhing about the bocadillo when our next dish arrived, it was the confit duck montadito, with black cherry and a la peral (cheese) spread, holy crap!! can you say orgasm with your mouth stuffed??? this was my favourite of the night (my wife preferred the boquerones). The feast was not over yet, as we next ordered pulpo (octopus), mussels and patatas asturianas. The pulpo delivered, not chewy and quite tender and flavorful, with a spicy tomato sauce and smoked olive aioli. Then came the mussels, which were actually the only reason i'm not giving this a 5 star. It came in a tomato sauce that was a bit on the salty side. We managed to eat it, because it was still quite good but it wasn't as perfect as the previous dishes. Our last savory course were the patatas, which by then we were almost to the brim, and compared to the rest of the food were not as exciting. I think it'd be best to order these early on in your meal. Don't get me wrong, they were still delicious with a cheesy cream poured tableside. Even though we were quite satisfied, we decided to share a dessert, and we opted for the toasted brioche with caramel and oranges, with a cava gelee and a creme fraiche ice cream, it was also very good! In all, it was a great experience, the dishes were brought to the table in a timely manner, well spread between each other so we didn't feel rushed. Service was friendly and you can tell that they have received good training (kudos for Chef Garces). Our bill came to $130 including tax + 20% tip and we both thought it was good vaule for the experience. Will definitely visit other Garces restaurants whilst in Philly!

text: Will preface with stating, maybe I am too picky, maybe I taste sweet more potently than most. Also as I try other items on menu, will update review as I realize my spouse and I can only eat so much each time and it won't be such a thorough review. However, I doubt we'd return to Fork. We had been wanting to try this place just for the convenient location and interesting online menu, but foodie friends had given lackluster reviews. Today was just so nice and sunny, yet windy enough to keep us cool that we decided to try the outside seating. Indeed, the weather was perfect for outside, given the lack of shade, except that the Hole is finally being worked on. Due to poor tarping, tiny styrofoam bits were blowing in, through, and upon the patio. yum. Once it gets hotter and less windy, look out! They will need some shade or trees and misting fans, because that is going to be stinking hot. Server very nice, timeliness of order taking, delivering, checking on all fine. Easy to be seated. Decided on the fried asparagus for starters, came with a very nice buttermilk ranch dipping sauce. I would say their frying oil temp is set too low, as the breading was greasy and not very crisp. Flavors good, asparagus was perfectly cooked. Despite that, so much grease = meh. Drinks: it is brunch, so ok for a few cocktails. Spouse got the bourbon-based 'old fashioned city bank.' This was a good combination, multiple ingredients but the bourbon still had good flavor. Too bad I'm not a bourbon fan, as my cocktail was too damn sweet and had hardly any alcohol. Mine was the 'Z's bucket,' a gin/berries/basil/lemon. Actually felt the flavor more like a pink lemonade with barely a shot of gin, in at least an 8oz glass. Disappointing and boring. In fact, ALL the cocktails on the list that didn't have bourbon (ok, leaving the mojito and the bloody mary off the list because I don't order those) came across as girlie drinks, and seemed likely to be super sweet. No adult drinks featuring liquor other than bourbon. Not adequate for me! Go to redfeather, get lamplighter. Husb had a burger with the rosemary/parm fries. The fries were good, he liked the burger, though the patty too small for the oversized bun. Since I am sooo picky..do go try this place if you at all want to, but below is the bulk of my negativity! I had the chicken corn chowder. For some reason I assumed the soup, listed as containing chicken, would not have bacon. I hate bacon/pancetta, I avoid pork and ham, but will eat if the flavor isn't overwhelming. Therefore if something lists bacon, I won't order. So I ordered the chowder, which doesn't list pork product on the menu. Oh look, has bacon. I didn't send back because...oh look, almost no bacon flavor. People! If it has bacon, you need to list it on the menu. DUH. And if you are going to use bacon, it needs to be enough to come across when the dish is eaten, otherwise it's a wasted ingredient, and there's the odd kosher person who will be pissed! Beyond the random flavor attempt, it came out not very hot. What was good was the large chicken chunks, the nice potatoes, and the corn flavor. I think it had some added thickener though, a little weird on the texture. I also ordered the cheese plank. The menu states: "*Northwest Cheese Plank 10.75 ~ assortment of local hand-crafted cheeses, local stone fruits, City Peanut Shop's spiced pecans & Ahaus Beehaus honey" Now you see where I'm a giant snob. This just looked sad. It wound up being about 1/2 oz manchego, a ~#50 scoop of chevre-type goat cheese, 1 oz hard goat, and 1 oz MILD white cheddar with some sort of truffle flavor. A few very thin slices of some local pear (this was so thin it rolled around the chevre fairly well, just not enough of it), probably 3 sliced up dried apricots, 3 small torched slices of bread (these crumbled to touch, wrong variety used), one very sad strawberry (but flavor good, especially for March). For the price, NOT WORTH IT. Go to Co-op, get better cheese, spend $3. Or even Freddy's, they have a surprising cheese selection. Oh, the spiced pecans were fine. Not super, sweet and spicy is about it. Maybe 2 tablespoons there. I was reluctant to order the cheese plate due to the bit about the truffle flavor, as I dislike truffle oil, but it actually didn't come through at all. This one was boring. text: Like many people, I like drinking - not like getting drinking to get drunk drinking, but drinking to have fun drinking. Lately, I have been working hard on my bourbon skills, buying way too much liquor and taking distillery tours. Kentucky is grand and all, but as a proud Tennessean, I have also toured both the Jack Daniels and Geroge Dickel distilleries. While they were both great, they were large and fairly impersonal affairs. But there is an alternative and it is right here in Nashville. I was recently privileged to take a private tour of the Corsair Artisan Distillery. Located in the old Yazoo Brewery location in the Marathon Motorworks building, the distillery shares its space (and equipment) with Collier and McKeel (who was coincidentally also there when I received my tour, making it extra great). The tour was conducted by one of the owners, Darek Bell, and was fascinating. Artisan prides itself on being rebel distillers (as opposed to Rebel Brewers, another great destination). They were busy at work making several of their varieties, including Rasputin Hopped Whiskey and Triple Smoke American Single Malt (for the snobby Scotch drinkers out there - single malt an Made In America!) When I was there they were also experimenting with a chamomile tea whiskey and a whiskey made from a traditional Russian beer recipe. Darek explained every step of the brewing and distilling process- how each phase works, what the machinery does and did so in prose that showed his bubbling passion, knowledge and love for the art and science (in his case, mad science) of distilling. Several times he consulted a book he is working on publishing which has recipes and showcases his mad distilling skills. Two items of extra special note were the copper still that had been saved throughout Prohibition by hiding out in a Kentucky barn and that is now proudly back in service (a find by Collier and McKeel I might add) and the small copper pipe (2' high x 3" around) complete distillery that Darek had made in order to produce small hand crafted batches of whiskey so he could perfect many of his extra-ordinary recipes. They have kept the Yazoo tasting room open, adding several other delicious beers as well (from Albita and he like) as well as an outside patio/courtyard. They also have a special room for private events and parties (they have even had a couple of weddings there). I don't know if they have any type of regularly scheduled tours set up, but if given the chance to go back, I would jump.

text: My craving for pizza kicked in last night. Big time. And I didn't just want a pan style or thin crust pizza, I wanted deep dish. A Chicago specialty and our personal favorite, we knew it was going to be a challenge finding a deep dish pizza in Saint Louis that not only had mozzarella cheese on it but tasted good as well. Racking my brain over places we've heard of we decided to try Pi, a popular and frequently talked about pizzeria in the area. They boast award winning deep dish, so we decided to see if they were worth their weight in pepperoni. We went to the Central West End location instead of driving to the burbs. When we got there, I was instantly impressed with the place. While I don't normally go for an uber trendy atmosphere, I really enjoyed the industrial meets modernesque feel. It was a bit on the dark side and very loud, but it was also Saturday night so it was really packed. We thought we would have to wait forever, but we were seated within 30 minutes. Not too shabby! Well, my impressed feeling slowly started to diminish as our night progressed. We both decided for some crazy reason to skip the booze and we ordered iced tea instead. Now, anytime we go to a restaurant and order tea we get plain old unsweetened tea. Not at Pi! We were served some sort of fruity, sweet raspberry-mango flavored "tea", and it was horrible. I'm not one to normally complain, but if you are going to serve this sort of drink to your patrons as the standard, let it be known. It wasn't on the menu, and out server didn't bring it up. Not everyone likes these kind of specialty drinks, so let your customers know what they are getting into before you bring it to them. I was belching fruity nastiness for the rest of the night. Even after I ate anchovies (I'll get to that!) We are wing fanatics, so when we saw blazed wings with blue cheese on the menu, we knew we had to try them. When they arrived, all I could think was WTF?? That's all I'm going to say! Captain Wow felt strongly enough about them that he's decided to break his silence and write about them himself. So, keep your eye out for his take on Pi and their "wings". By this point, I was really starting to get worried. We ordered the deep dish pizza with pepperoni, roasted red peppers, banana peppers...and I added anchovies to my half. Yes, anchovies. It's an acquired taste, don't be judging! When the pie arrived my first impression was, that is not deep dish pizza! I mean, it looked right, but it was so tiny compared to what we are used to that it reminded me of a doughy pan style pizza instead. We both took a slice and dug in, and praise Jebus it actually tasted ok! They didn't give us the roasted red peppers and put raw green pepper on instead, and they really skimped on toppings in general, but it had a nice crust and the sauce was really good. It had a nice spicy sweet flavor, and the crust was cooked well. Still, it was no where near Chicago style deep dish. I realize that things are done differently in STL and I won't get food like back home all the time, but if you boast award winning pizza, you better deliver. This was just another pizza to me. It had some good flavors going, but just cannot compete with Gino's back home or the Captain's homemade version. I will say that the service was very good, and everyone was nice. They only serve a few appetizers, salads, and a few desserts in addition to the deep dish or thin crust pizza, so if pizza is not your thing this will not be the place for you. Prices were a bit high for what we got, but we were also in a more upscale neighborhood so it was expected. I think Pi's issue is that they are going for a more trendy, urbanized experience than being focused on the food itself. They have a huge bar and serve several speciality drinks and cocktails, and you could tell it was a hot spot for meeting up with friends to drink and socialize. Which is awesome, if you like that sort of thing. I will admit that the decor, funky music and eclectic clientele sucked me in at first, but in the end it's all about the food. The pizza here is lacking, and that's a shame because I really want to like this place. Maybe a return visit during lunch or one of the suburb locations would be an improvement? I don't know. It would take some convincing to get us to eat here again. Eating STL, A Chicago Perspective http://eatingstl.blogspot.com/

text: I guess when you get to the point where you are the Duke or Duchess of a business, you should review them. Let me say that all of my yelp check in's at Sam's have been sitting waiting at the fuel pump for my car to fill up. If you live in Franklin, this is the cheapest place to buy gas, so I'm here at least weekly. It's reality when you live here and work in Nashville. And what else are you going to do waiting for the "click?" We do shop at Sam's in the store frequently, hubby usually does that part - and they do have some deals. I understand one other yelper's comments about how they used to be REALLY cheap, and now not so much. But to that point I say, the world is a smaller place. The purchasing in quantity idea, not as prevalent anymore. I've always known that it was cheaper to purchase soft drinks by the case at the grocery - Pepsi and Coke strongly incentivize that. We buy our "household" products (detergents, paper towels, etc.) here because it is at least as cheap as buying on sale at the grocery, and I don't have to worry about running out of TP with guests in the house. For my everyday lotion, Sam's is significantly cheaper than the grocery, Walgreen's, or Target... and for generic drugs you take every day - definitely check them out. Is Sam's cheaper than Costco? I don't know. Our family business buys a Sam's merchandise, we use Discover, so that's our choice. If you are an American Express person or debit card-er, and maybe you live closer to Costco, then go there. I have purchased several GREAT deals finding out of season merchandise (or about to be out of season) here, so when you are searching for patio furniture, holiday items, etc. - don't overlook them. Also store displays you can really negotiate hefty discounts for blemishes, etc. As I look around our house - our patio set (10 pieces, we have a large deck), dining table and six chair set, and an upholestered recliner have all come from there. So yes, I'd say we're a fan.

text: This was a big disappointment. Twice. I usually like to give a place the benefit of the doubt if they aren't great the first time around. I could have saved myself the effort on this place though. I have two guidelines when ordering in places like this. First, order what they put their name on. In this case, The Toni Roni Special pizza. The second is that if a restaurant wins anything for a menu item (even the popularity contest that is the Best of Philly), it's worth a try. Working from the bottom up, since it's the dough that makes a pizza, you have a soft and floppy center. If you've ever taken an Elio's pizza out of the toaster oven about halfway through cooking, it's like that. Sure, it's edible if you're really hungry but it doesn't support the weight of the sauce, cheese and toppings and just folds over, dumping said cheese and toppings on your plate. The outer crust was ok. If the whole pizza had that crispness, it might have been a serviceable pie. The sauce is ok, I can't complain about anything there. The toppings though were bland and generally under done. The sausage looked it was steamed or boiled. There's no excuse for that when you have a grill. Like I said, I do like to give a place a 2nd chance so naturally I went with one of their tomato pies since it was voted Best of Philly. Sometimes less is more, this was one of those times. I ordered the Sinatra which is one of their tomato pie with mozzarella and basil on the top. Sounds great, right? Starting from the bottom up again, the crust was very crisp, almost hard and brittle. Ok, it's not what I'm used to but it was ok. Although it was sort of like eating a bowl of captain crunch, the roof of your mouth gets scraped up a bit. Still, it was tasty, I just wish it had a little more body to it. The sauce was pretty good, it had some texture to it, some real tomato and not just a paste, which was nice. The mozzarella though was bland and rubbery and the slices were about the size of quarters, maybe a half dollar. The idea was good but it's a total waste to put low quality cheese on a decent pizza. So that's that, I won't be going back again, ever.

text: The Greater Reno Grub and Gripe Group gathered at Asian Noodles for some delicious Asian fondue and it certainly seems worth bringing to the attention of other foodies. Asian Noodles is in the Costco shopping center in Reno and has expanded into the business next door. About a month ago it added the fondue. The all-you-can-eat fondue starts with a broth you use to cook your vegetables, protein and noodles. You get two. We choose yellow curry and a Thai tom yum made from lemon grass. Both were tasty. They bring the broth out and put it on an electric heater. You can pick as many meats, vegetables and noodles as you want. They bring it out one dish at a time. So if you order more, it doesn't mean you get more. You get smaller amounts of each. Just about everything worked well. The vegetables seemed especially fresh and tasty. We tried something called ton ho, which I guess are chrysanthemum leaves. There were three kinds of mushrooms and all worked well, but the enoki mushrooms were probably the best. The fried tofu and sliced bamboo shoots were also stand outs for me. The beef, chicken, pork and lamb were also tasty. I think the beef worked best for me. It was pretty much like the beef used in tai pho. The seafood is where we seemed to run into problems. I liked the sliced fish and squid balls. Both the shrimp and mussels had fishy tastes to me. They offer three kinds of noodles but we tried only glass noodles and the yellow noodles. I liked the yellow noodles but the glass noodles were the clear winner here (no pun intended). You can either eat your food as a soup or you can use the basket scoop they provide to pull out stuff to eat without broth. I look forward to going back and trying the fondue with other broths. This would be a great way to eat with vegetarian friends, by the way. They offer a vegetarian broth and the vegetables and noodles alone would be tasty enough. The spicy herbal broth and the miso broth also look promising. They have a plain soup base, an herbal broth, and, for extra money, a goat soup broth as well. Service was good. The Asian fondue is $20 a person and given the quality of the ingredients well worth the price.

You have the option of putting a dry rub or a wet rub on your chicken. Torn between the dry rub and the wet rub, I went with my first inclination and ordered the harrissa dry rub. On the surface, chicken and donuts seem like an odd combination, but they pair together well, just like chicken and waffles. text: Update 5/9/12 Stopped by again with a family member and the food was great. It was their first visit and they gave it a big thumbs up for taste and couldn't get over the large portions. Whatever happened on the visit where the rice was dry is history, so I'm raising my score back up to 5 stars. Update 4/21/12 Back again to check out other menu items and see how they did on the fried rice (after my last visit - see below). Came on late Saturday night, and it was not too busy. Ordered the shrimp and broccoli and upgraded to shrimp fried rice. The shrimp and broccoli was excellent, again with a light sauce letting the ingredients shine through. Definitely one of the better takeout meals I've had in the area. With the upgrade to shrimp fried rice, it had good portions of shrimp, and the moisture and flavors were back to the solid standard from my first time, and definitely not dry like my last visit. Only thing I can point to for the difference may be the times I visited? When the rice was dry it was a bit after lunch. Perhaps their rice in the vessel had dried out after the lunch traffic? Could be. Both times the rice was good it was off-hours and slow traffic. On the other hand, this meal had the shrimp fried rice upgrade, and of course, it was freshly made vs. the standard pork fried rice. Whatever the reason, this meal had the problem solved, and I'm upgrading to shrimp fried rice from now on. And the fact I've been here 3 times in about a week because of the excellent flavors speaks for itself. I'm still holding my overall score at 4 stars until I'm wowed again a few times. ----------------------------- Update 4/19/12: Came back for more Chinese since I had been so pleased just a few days before. Had the Szechuan beef again and it was just as good, but the pork fried rice was far too dry. As in, "I can't believe this is the same place," kind of dry. Not sure what happened as I ate at lunchtime both days and it was never that busy each day. I did try the pan fried dumplings and they were small, but tasty. I'm dropping my food score to 4 (the rice was actually a 2), and overall score to 4 based on the rice. If a Chinese takeout place can't do fried rice consistently well, it's disappointing. I'm sure I'll be back in a few days to try it again and will update my review then. ----------------------------- My new favorite Chinese takeout place! I have no idea how this place escaped me in my Yelp searches for this area. Fortunately I was talking Chinese takeout with a good friend, and he said, "Say no more, we're going to China Garden for lunch tomorrow!" And am I glad we did. China Garden has been open since 2000 and it located on McMullen Booth, in the large plaza on the west side between 590 and Drew St. It's in a small store right in the middle of the plaza and can be a bit hard to find with all the retail stores surrounding it. But it's definitely worth the search, and you'll be richly rewarded. The interior is modest, but very clean and neat, and the menu is large and has typical offerings priced well. And the owner that took our order was very kind and attentive. There are about 90 items on the menu including apps, soup and fried rice. The remaining dinners are well priced at ~$8-10 for a large order. They also have about 30 dinner combos at $7-8, ~15 chef's specialties at $9-12. But the huge hit is their ~30 lunch specials (with pork fried rice or white rice) priced at $4.50-5.25. I've found no Chinese restaurant that serves this quality for such a great price, and the my plate was covered with a healthy serving. I ordered the Szechuan beef which you can choose with your level of heat. I kept it standard (average heat) as it was my first time, and the heat was perfect. In appropriate time our orders landed on the table. China Garden is one of those rare Chinese takeout restaurants that doesn't oversauce their dishes. One thing I look for in all Asian food is a light hand on the sauce, with a delicateness of flavor where each ingredient shines through, and the sauce doesn't overwhelm the dish but rather pulls all the flavors together. On this measure, China Garden is off the charts compared to other places I've tried in the area. The Szechuan sauce was quite flavorful, but never once did it mask the taste of the ingredients, which were quite fresh and blended well. As to value, China Garden is excellent. My lunch plate completely filled me up for $4.50. A fast food place could hardly do it for that price, and the ingredients would not be near as healthy. I'll definitely be back to China Garden the next time I'm in the mood for Chinese. My ratings on the local Chinese takeout scale are: Atmosphere: 4 Service: 5 Food: 5 Value: 5

text: How did Sopapillas get "Best Overall" and "Best Mexican" designations in the Toast of Music City? How did it get good reviews on Yelp? It's a mystery to me, but it was enough to lure me into this this place. The meal did not get off to a good start, when we were told to wait despite the visibly empty tables because they were "short handed." We declined to wait in the bar but when we were seated--that's where they put us. With music blaring AND the football game on the tv, the cacophony of noise was such that we could barely carry on a conversation. As it turns out, the only topic of conversation during the meal was how disappointing the food was. I love New Mexican cuisine, and was so looking forward to this meal. But as I found out, the only thing authentic about the food at Sopapillas may be the chili rellenos, because they evidently are shipped in from New Mexico. Unfortunately the shipment must not have arrived for this weekend's diners, because I was told they were "all out" at 4:30 on Saturday. The waiter assured us that everything else was made fresh in the kitchen. So, I ordered the tamale instead. I have never had a tamale that did not have a filling. Tasting as if it were made from Martha White cornbread mix, the only flavors were sweet (yes, sweet) and a hint of green chili in the middle of what was otherwise just three inches of mushy cornbread mix. The beef taco that I asked to accompany the tamale (and which would have come with the chili relleno rather than the shrimp taco that comes with the tamale platter usually) was shredded beef with no spice at all, sitting in a fried flour tortilla, which by the time the plate came to me, was lying on its side long enough for that side to be totally moist and limp. The only flavor came from the small bit of pico de gallo on the side. The side dish of black beans was equally bland. Did their shipment of spices and herbs also get lost? My dining partner's enchilada contained some shredded chicken with no flavor topped with just the tiniest bit of sauce. The only thing we enjoyed, as other reviewers have noted, was the flavorful salsa, but it must be scooped up with cold, cardboard like chips. The guacomole might have been good, but for $10 we did not think it was worth trying. To top off this lackluster meal, two pillows of grease were set down in front of us without a word from our waiter (or maybe he mumbled something I couldn't hear.) I usually LOVE sopapillas. The oil on these pretenders oozed out on to my fingers when I touched them. I have never seen that much grease on anything that was served in a restaurant. OK, they were free. But I'm still not going to eat them. Two stars for trying.

text: Maxine's is one of our favorite places to go for Saturday or Sunday brunch. They have soul food at a good price. You can't really beat it. I recently was in Atlanta, GA and wanted to try a chicken and waffles place there called Gladys Knight's Chicken and Waffles. I had really high expectations for Atlanta soul food, given that we were in the south! There was a long wait (obviously a very popular place) and we finally were seated. The food was a little cheaper (although, we found that all the food in Atlanta was cheaper than Indianapolis). There were 4 of us and all of us were used to Maxine's in Indy. Anyway, we all got chicken and waffles to try. I am happy to say that Maxine's blew Gladys Knight's chicken and waffles out of the water! Like, I said, we had expected the south to have just killer soul food, but instead we discovered that Maxines is just damn good and hard to beat. Put it this way, I don't like fried chicken. It's messy, greasy, unhealthy. But, I honestly enjoy the thin crispy, well seasoned chicken wings at Maxines. If you are first timer, you have to go for the chicken and waffles (there is a waffle and 1 chicken wing option on their $5 menu....better for smaller appetites). I really enjoy the biscuit and gravy off the $5 menu...I can never finish it, but it's sure tasty. I also like the fact that maxine's doesn't have pork products since I prefer turkey bacon anyway. Their waffles are wonderful. They are thick and they come with peach butter which is amazing. You can get several different flavors and you can even get "half and half." I recommend the sweet potato waffle--tastes like a cinnamon waffle. Mac and Cheese is pretty good...cheesy, but typical. The Greens...now those are spectacular. Tons of flavor, even a bit spicy! YUM! Service can be hit or miss. They are always friendly, but sometimes it's pretty slow. I think one of the problems is that the kitchen (stove in particular) is not really large enough to accomodate...or they need another one. They certainly make you feel like you are at home though! We find the best service is when the "Big Man" is there. I'm not sure what his name is but Im guessing he's one of the owners and things seem to flow quite smoothly when he's around. He's like a big Teddy bear! Thank you Maxine's for bringing killer soul food to Indianapolis!

text: When I found out there was a new micro brewery in town I got very excited. I finally got time to get over to RGB and sample some of their brew. Location The location is great for business and there is plenty of parking within walking distance. We walked in the door and there was a good local band playing for us to enjoy. So far so good. It was quiet busy but we were lucky to get two seats at the bar. Bar itself: Once seated we started to look at the beer list and the place itself. The bar itself was very bland and seemed sterile. White walls and not much decor to speak of. Sitting at the bar was comfortable and you weren't getting bumped into while sitting there. The tap room was right in front of us in plain view. It wasn't the tap room I am accustom to with the beautiful stainless steel kettles lined up with kegs and bottles waiting for beer. It had smaller kettles and a large plastic fermenter and some other random things laying around. This isn't a big deal, I can look past it. The staff: The staff were friendly but seemed disconnected. They were hard to strike a conversation with and it felt awkward when speaking with them. When asking about the beers, I thought they would have known more. I am not sure if they were just a bartender or were a brewer but that was a bit of a disappointment. Lets get on to what really matters The Beer! The Beer: In order to give them the proper judgement, I ordered a 5oz sample of all 8 beers they had on tap that night. Started with 4 and sipped lightest to darkest. The Oktoberfest wasn't bad, not the best I have ever had but it was one of the better of the 4. Blackback IPA was the star of these 4 samples but it was not as bitter and strong as I was hoping. The other 2 beers were down right forgettable. Something I did notice was that the beers did not have much of an aroma. When tasting new brews I love to test the aroma and get the hoppy notes and sweetness of the malts. I didn't get any of this. On to the second 4 samples. Again I go for the aroma...not much to be had. Two of the lighter beers tasted almost identical. I could tell there was a difference in the bitterness but overall the same taste and look. The gluten free beer was next, it was tasty for a gluten free. The last was the Saison, which the bartender put syrup in. Now I am not a Saison person but this beer was not very good at all. Overall the beer was forgettable and sub par. When asked will I come back? I would only say yes because they didn't have all of there beers on tap. I would come back and try others when they are available. Otherwise I will not come back until I hear that they are making some serious beers for the enthusiast. Simple breakdown. Location = Good Bar = bland and a sterile feel Staff = Disconnected and awkward Beer = Sub-par

text: I was a little hesitant to try this place, considering the yelp reviews so far have been very hit or miss, and because someone said that the veggie burger was so gross that they literally spit it out. But vegetarians have different tastes (take my sis and I for example), so we decided to give it a shot. They have a lot of communal seating downstairs, and some along the windows upstairs as well, which I'm not crazy about. I don't care to know strangers' business, and frankly, I don't care to be smooshed up against them while I'm trying to eat either. Luckily, my sis and I went on a Saturday afternoon, and they weren't crazy busy, so we actually got a two-top upstairs. And there wasn't too much eating going on anyway, but more on that later. So our waitress came by after about 5 minutes and took our drink orders. My sis tried to order the root beer on draft, but apparently they don't even have one on draft, even though it clearly states that they do both on their drink menu in the restaurant and on the website. They only have a few bottled root beers, and those are at least 2 dollars each with no refills. So she just stuck with water, and I got the Lucky diet coke on draft, which was good, but unnecessary considering this place was one of the coldest places I've ever eaten in. By the time we left, my hands were icicles. And I didn't even order ice cream! If you want to encourage people to do so, especially in 50 degree weather, you might want to splurge for some heat. When we ordered our food, I asked the waitress what was in the veggie burger, and she said "nuts, garbanzo beans, and lots of veggies." Yum! Sounds promising! So my sis ordered that as is (with jicama slaw, avocado mouse, and queso fresco) and I subbed a veggie burger into the basic (with ketchup, mayo, lettuce, tomato, and onions) with no tomato, extra sauce, and add white cheddar. We both also ordered fries with their homemade"catsup," as well as a side of housemade pickles for me and coleslaw for her. She mentioned that she doesn't do onions though, so if they come in the slaw or jicama slaw, she didn't want them. The waitress said that she was 90% sure they didn't, and that was that. Our food was out fairly quickly, and right away, I noticed how unappetizing the veggie burger looked. It didn't appear to be cooked, was cold, and while mine had basically no mayo or "catsup" on it, my sister's had a mound of what else? Onion slaw. And her coleslaw was chalk full of not only red onions but a topper of scallions as well. At least the fries and pickles looked good! My sister and I have opposite tastes. I mean, besides not eating meat, we never agree on anything. But we both took one bite of that veggie burger, and sure enough, it was gross. Inedible. It wasn't full of veggies. It was full of undercooked, under-spiced pinto beans. And that's it. I couldn't even eat the pickles I had put on top of it at this point. And when you waste my pickles, I am one unhappy camper. My sister said that we should say something, and I agreed. So we told our waitress. And then we waited. And waited. And waited some more. After probably 15 minutes, our waitress came back to tell us that our burgers were being taken care of. But the manager never came over. And neither did Dave Bailey, who was downstairs, and not all that busy. Our waitress also identified herself as a vegetarian, but said that she had never tried the veggie burger. Shame that he never had the staff taste the food first in order to be helpful to both the customers, and to himself as well. I ate my sister's onion...I mean coleslaw, and some fries, which were good, and she had fries and ice cream, but we still left 20 dollars poorer, hungry, cold, and downright mad. I've eaten pretty much every veggie burger in the Saint Louis area. Fozzie's makes their own, as does the Bleeding Deacon, and OR Juice and Smoothie, which are all delish. I've even had them at Burger King! That's right...they serve veggie burgers, and they are way better than Bailey's Range. You don't have to pay for ketchup and mustard, which, homemade or not, is downright ludicrous in a burger joint. And frankly, they have better service too, because if I ever had to complain there, at least the manager or the owner would care enough to come over.
