text: I love to go shopping at the Co-op...when I can afford it! Having been a vegetarian for 14 years, I certainly learned to appreciate the foods that most people find gross or unpleasant like tempeh, tofu, seaweed, and wheat grass. If you're a weirdo like me in that case, you'll love this store for its wide selection of both local and more commercial organic and healthy-type foods. This was the only place in Tucson that I was able to get my favorite kind of soy jerkey for years. Sometimes, Id grab one of their Tempeh BLT's from their deli fridge for a quick lunch (theres loads of great stuff in there!). And although I rarely bought any, their fresh daily made soups are pretty darn good. I love the fact that you can buy LOCAL, Organic produce here. Ive had a few opportunities to discuss with the man in charge there and firstly, its important to know that they pay fair rates for local produce. Its good to know that the people putting in the hard work for the crop are getting paid good money for it. They dont take a huge cut for themselves, and prices wind up being reasonable considering you can call the farmer yourself (or just ask an employee there) about what nutrients and fertilizers were used in the making of your food. I just love the idea of helping out the little guy, too. So much so that I have heavily considered becoming a specialty organic tomato supplier for them in the past! Who knows? Maybe some day I will! I sure wont be able to eat ALL those san marzanos and black heirlooms by myself. Last thing I go here for when I really plan on treating myself is loose leaf tea. This is one of the best tea selections Ive ever seen, and anyone who enjoys the stuff in its true form rather than those crappy little bagged things will really be appreciative of the Co-op. I wish their prices for some items were lower, but the quality you get with most of their stuff is just so far any beyond anywhere else, it makes it worth the price. Love it, will return as frequently as my wallet will allow.

text: Yes Artmart is overpriced, I admit that wholeheartedly. I still love every inch of the store, however, and if I won the lottery, i would probably buy everything housed within its kooky, creative exterior. It's truly an artist paradise - as long as you're not the "starving" kind of artist and have a great bank account, extensive credit limit and a stable income (preferably of the trust fund variety) to support yourself. Artmart has everything any artist could ever want (or never knew they needed). Paint brushes of every size, shape and conceivable bristle type, canvases, paint colors and brands as far as the eye can see, sketch pads, markers (including my favorites: Copics from Japan), pens, pencils, charcoal, airbrush equipment, calligraphy pens, different types of paper, masking tapes, erasers, watercolors, easels, instruction manuals, mini human figures to use for posing, lights for still lifes, cards, stamps, ink, I could go on for days. In addition to all the artist goodies and doodads, Artmart also has its own framing section so you put your masterpiece under glass with any kind of frame you can think of. And be forewarned, it's not cheap. But when you have that one of a kind [insert your name here], only the best will do: only the most unique frame, the best mat and the finest glass (or plexiglass). And they can accommodate that request. Multiple, multiple books of frames, pieces of frames, mats in every color of the rainbow, and various types of glass are available for your viewing and choosing pleasure. And I almost forgot to mention the little last minute time-wasters in your direct path as you approach the cash registers: the Gelly Roll pens, mini books on subjects like Zen Gardens, funny mustache shaped magnets, cardboard babies and greeting cards just too clever to pass up. Artmart is a black hole for your wallet. And I love, love, love it every time I go in. It's so much fun, but here's a tip if you're afraid of going into severe debt as you walk out the doors laden down with a new airbrush kit, calligraphy set, 36-pack of markers and 18 canvases "On sale today only!": leave your wallet locked in the car. Went back this week when they were open, they had 4 of their beers available. We got a sampler and the best they had was not something I would buy. I mean, I do not mean this place any ill will, I think the taproom itself looks awesome, and if they served anything I would drink, I would be there. It's really rare I won't finish something... Forgetting what one of the beers was called, I just called it "trust fund ale" as that's the only way I could figure the place spawned. It definitely wasn't from the beer. I can't think that a bunch of people said "hey, this beer's so good you should start a brewery" - I think someone said "hey, let's start a brewery and how hard could it be to brew beer?" I would love for them to succeed, but I think that's going to take committing someone to brewing at least one decent beer, and having the place open a lot more than it is now. As it stands, it's a picture of what a bar should be... and by picture, I mean it looks good and tastes like developing fluid. I do like the fact that food trucks come and park outside the place. text: In my constant searching for good Mexican/Central American food here in Central NJ, I came across this place on hiddentrenton.com. It is the sister restaurant to Taqueria El Mariachi up on Olden. They're doing it right at this restaurant, which I would categorize as a hybrid of Mexican and Guatemalan. Chips with a very fresh and generous serving of guacamole were a bargain at $3.95. Wife, daughter and I split an order of carne asada tacos, tacos al pastor (both items were 3 tacos for $6.50) and cheese pupusas (3 for $6.00). The taco platters, made with soft corn tortillas, were generously filled and garnished with lime wedges and grilled green onions. I have to say, short of a taco truck I visited in Brooklyn some time back, this may be the closest to proper carne asada I've had in the Northeast. My wife and daughter preferred the tacos al pastor, which were tender, juicy and marinated in something delicious. Plate of pupusas was as big as my face, with delectable edges of browned crunchy cheese, topped with seasoned & pickled shredded cabbage with carrots. There were 3 salsas on the table; a mild, tomato-y sauce, salsa verde mixed with avocado, and a spicier deep red salsa with dusky, hot overtones; all were excellent. The mild sauce on the pupusas created delicious little ad hoc latino grilled cheese bites with a tomato soup finish. Little girl had a strawberry shake; wife and I each had a glass of iced horchata, which is not a common find in this neck of the woods. It tasted as if the horchata was fresh - not corn-syrupy sweet like you find it in some taquerias. Big thumbs up for this place; highly recommended. Our bill including tax was just a little over $29. The Chambersburg location is much more inviting than the one up on Olden, and the interior is cheerier. Street parking, cash only. They don't have a license for booze, but did have racks of wine glasses, so I'd assume BYO is fine; I'd call ahead to make sure.

It was pure creamy deliciousness, served with toasted sourdough bread. Amazing. As an entree, my boyfriend ordered fish and chips as it is his favorite at Dandelion. It was a great dish as usual aside from the fact that he only got one piece of fish. I ordered the lamb bolognese even though I hate lamb. I figured, if anyone is going to make me love a dish with lamb, it is Starr, and I was proven right. It was served with orecchiette pasta, and the whole dish was truly incredible. It had chucks of carrots (a true bolognese) and there was a ton of meat (I hate when they skimp on the meat when you order bolognese). We were so stuffed after our meal that we skipped dessert but ordered another round of drinks. Overall, another great experience at a Starr restaurant, and I cant wait for the next time!

text: Went to Chappy's this week on business. My co-workers had really hyped this place so I was pretty psyched. I've spent a lot of time in New Orleans so was really excited about authenitc cajun cuisine. The ambiance was pretty blah. Nothing too exciting, Walls were very plain. Would have expected more NOLA themes around the place. We were there at 6 and the place was fairly empty. Even then, service was generally slow. The menu is generous, with most entree's in the $20-25 range. For appetizers, we ordered crab cakes, blackened shrimp and tuna tar tare for the table of 6. The crab cakes were very good (and that's saying a lot for a Maryland native!). They weren't Maryland style lump, but they were tasty, seasoned well and cooked perfectly. The shrimp overcooked and salty, which was truly foreshadowning of the rest of the meal. Even the tuna had a very salty rub on the exterior. For my entree, I ordered the blackened redfish, which was recommended by one of my co-workers. As described int he menu: "marinated in butter, sprinkled with Chappy's spices, pan fried to perfection and served with maMAma's shrimp and eggplant." I asked if the fish could be just grilled, without the butter, but the server recommended against it. Though the fish itself was cooked perfectly, nice and flaky, I'd swear there was a pound of salt in the rub. The shrimp and eggplant side was the highlight of the dinner -- very tasty. This was a company meal with locals that loved the place, so I didn't complain, but this wasn't close to the meals I've had in the French Quarter or, in most other cajun places in other place. You know how sometimes you have a meal that you're disappointed with but chalk it up to a bad night so you'll try it again? Well, this isn't one of them. I'm sure there are better places in Music City next time I'm there.

The staff is very friendly and free breakfast (coffee, tea, juice and DELICIOUS baked goods) is available in the tiny office every morning. Nice sense of style, very affordable (I think we paid about $90 a night), within walking distance of State Street and away from how loud it can sometimes get (although you can still hear a lot of traffic noise, so bring earplugs). One thing we really appreciated was the book in the room with a list of recommendations for local bars, restaurants, etc. We checked out many of them and found every one worth visiting! Overall, I loved the vibe of this hotel. But the one area it was short on was comfort. text: I've eaten here three times: twice for dinner and once for the buffet. I totally don't agree that this is the "best in Indy." I think it's fairly similar to other Northern Indian restaurants like Shalimar or India Garden--but with a fatal flaw. Read on. THE GOOD For dinner, they bring out tasty papad and chutney. For dinner and lunch, they bring out a generous basket of piping hot nan. It's A- nan in my book, but it's fresh (unlike the nan of many other establishments who leave the bread to languish on the buffet). The food is of pretty good quality. The staff is cheery and attentive. So what's not to dig? THE BAD The food is SALTY, man! It just destroys me. My girlfriend and I split a fish pakora and a goat curry for dinner recently, and I think we lowered the water table because we were drinking so much. Crying out for ¡EL AGUA! Yes, Indian food is not usually your first choice for low-sodium fare. But having half an appetizer and entree and feeling that bad is unacceptable. It's a shame, as their food is pretty well-prepared, otherwise. For example, the ajwain seeds in the fish pakora were a nice touch (by the way, I think the majority of the saltitude was in the curry, not the pakora). THE BUFFET People have given the lunch buffet high marks. I had it today and was unimpressed. There was no more variety than at your typical Indian joint in town. There were no dishes that really blew me away. It was just average--except SALTIER than average. (In fact, I tested out the buffet today even after my previous, salty experiences precisely because so many people were lauding it.) For Indian food in Indy, I recommend Passage to India (my favorite--vegetarian with lots of Southern food, great soups), India Palace (huge lunch buffet with substantial meat dishes), Taj of India (simple but good quality for lunch or dinner), and Shalimar (decent lunch buffet, nice dinner service with good thali).

They offer great deals during the week for students but if you're going on a Saturday or Sunday be prepared to pay full price. text: Wow. This is not our normal type of bar so I'm not going to review the decor, music, or the bathrooms. My review would be totally biased. Let's talk about the customer service and the food, shall we? Last year I won $100 Cavanaugh's Cash at a charity fundraising event. Neat right? Free beer! Well the gift certificates were expired a year before the actual event. Event: October 2010, Expiry: September 2009. The event organizers called Cavanaugh's and let them know about the misprint, and Cavanaugh's signed off on them, crossing off the expiry date and someone left their initials. Sweet. So fast forward to today, when we want to use the $100. Since we don't normally frequent this place, I called ahead just to make sure that whoever's initials were included next to the crossed off expiry date were valid, blah, blah, blah. (I didn't want to rack up a huge bill to find out they wouldn't accept the gift cards.) I spoke to an EXTREMELY rude person on the phone who was huffing and puffing about, "Well I don't recognize those initials." (This is why I called ahead...) I was cool with her, and told her what event I won them at and she finally said, "Fine bring them in." And HUNG UP ON ME. Really? Hung up on me? We go in anyway and again, not our type of bar, but whatever, we were going to get a few rounds of beers and food with a friend. We go to pay our bill which was $76.30. Now, at every single other eating establishment that I've been to, if you don't spend the entire card, they'll cut you another one for the difference. They won't give cash back, for obvious reasons, and we weren't expecting that. We left a generous $16 tip IN CASH (more than 20%). When we asked for the difference to be put on another card we got eye rolling and more sighing and huffing and puffing. We were told by a pissed off manager who acted like we were scum of the earth (what did we do wrong again?), "It clearly states NO CHANGE back." We explained calmly that we weren't expecting cash back. After nearly three minutes of the manager rolling her eyes at us, she cut us another certificate for $23.70. At which point we handed it to another patron because there was no way we were coming back. (I really hope she enjoyed the fact that their bill was $23.70 cheaper!) Now, if Cavanaugh's want to state on the cards, "Must spend the entire amount of the gift certificate in one seating," that's one thing. But it did not say that. Even if that's what their non-stated policy is, they could have come to our table and said, "Hey guys, you may want to order another round of drinks because you're short and we can't give you a card for the difference." That would have been totally fine (albeit weird). Instead we were treated like trash. It will be also noted that we went in on a Sunday afternoon, the place was NEARLY empty so we weren't bothering anyone during a rush period. We also thought our 20+% cash tip would go a long way to our server who probably had a very slow afternoon. She wasn't a phenomenal server, but I've worked at bars before so I know what it's like to live on tips and how much slow days can really suck. With service like this from the manager, I'm not surprised the place was so empty. Food: If you enjoy airport-pub type food this place might be your thing. Salad consisted of iceberg lettuce, tomatoes and shaved carrots. Really? That's what Denny's was serving 20 years ago. We weren't expecting much, but it was pretty bad for Philadelphia. In a city where there seems to be an amazing gastropub on every corner (offering far better food at similar prices), this place just does not meet the standard of most of the bars in Philly. Beers on tap were pretty good, I'll give them that. My advice? If you appreciate eye-rolling and boring, predictable food, this might be your ticket. I won't be going back. Not even for $23.70 of free drinks.

These tasty sandwiches were delicious and satisfyingly filling. There are also a few squeeze sauce bottles on the table for your seasoning pleasure - one is a red picante sauce which is pretty hot & spicy and the other is a milder creamy green sauce - both sauces were good. text: Damn, this place is too legit to quit! Was tired of my usual lunch fare at work and decided to see what all else is in the neighborhood of Page Ave. Discovered both this place and Las Palmas within 2 minutes away from me. So I figured it was time to try something. I am glad I picked Durango instead of Las Palmas though. It was really authentic and fresh! Like others have mentioned, this restaurant is akin to the places on Cherokee Street. I got lost finding it though, oddly enough. It's on Page, and for some reason my Yelp app direction thing told me to go on Page Industrial....hmm. It's also right next to a Mexican grocery store, and you have to go in the third door on the right, not the first or second or you will end up in the grocery store. It happened to me, and it was kinda awkward. Also Durango is pretty much a seat yourself place, which I didn't know either, so I stood there for a minute or so looking stupid until I confirmed with a waitress that you just sit where-ever. Each table has a numbered card and they use that to keep track of what food you order. Almost immediately, a guy brought over some chips and two salsas and took my order. The chips weren't warm, but they still tasted delicious. The red salsa was A-FREAKIN-MAZING! Seriously, soooo good. The salsas were in those squeeze-y cylindrical ketchup holders, only they were clear with the tips chopped off for easy squirting, and damn...I went through 1/2 of a full one! It was that good. I wanted to drink it. I might have drank it. Eeew. :P The green salsa was WAY too spicy so I didn't touch it. I ordered the lengua tacos (beef tongue), carnitas (pork tips), and the buche tacos (pork stomach.) What is it with me and offal?! anyway! The tongue tacos were the besssst. Unnnfff. So tender and meaty. The stomach had good flavor but was reallly chewy and it reminded me of octopus which I don't much care for due to the chewiness of it. The pork tips were great too, nice and tender. I'd probably order them again, same with the tongue. Next time I wanna try the tripe though! I also got a side of rice and beans and guacamole. All of it was good, although the rice was lacking in flavor but I just fixed this by adding copious amounts of salsa. Mmmmm! The beans tasted great and they had cheese on top. I was the only female in the entire restaurant at lunch. It was mildly awkward. Also I didn't realize you paid at the register until I saw a line forming so I felt silly for asking for a check. No check came, so I went to wait in line to pay. They do take credit cards, so yay! I paid about $9.50 for my whole meal. Three tacos, beans, rice, guacamole, and the free chips. Not bad! I think I would definitely return, especially because it's so close and so fast (if you don't get lost.) Beef tongue. Mmmmm!

text: I moved to SE Arizona two years ago from the Pacific Northwest, and one of the things I miss most about Seattle is that there are so many Ethiopian restaurants there. I have been to Zeenams about 3 times and while I feel it's decent, I am not a fan of their injera. After hearing them mentioned on a local radio station, I made a beeline for Cafe Desta a week later when I was back in town. Cafe Desta's injera is -wonderful-, amongst the best I've had. I plan to go back and try more dishes, but I had the mild Lamb T'ibs and one of my favorite vegetable dishes, a cabbage/potato/carrot stew seasoned with ginger and tumeric called Ye'Atakilt Alich'a: it was perfect and simply flavorful like it should be. First I was hoping to try the Kitfo, a rather unusual 'meat tartare' sort of dish unique to this region's cooking, but I was told that the person who makes the best Kitfo was not cooking today so instead I should try the T'ibs. I was a bit hesitant to try them spicy, and will next time. They were tender and perfectly cooked, but pretty much straight lamb and onions to my palate...very good lamb though! Reading the other reviews, I must add that all my dishes were fresh and hot. I also had a guava juice and was surprised to see it was definitely not a tiny little glass, again nice to be getting reasonable portions for the cost. In Seattle, many Ethiopian restaurants are much less expensive (perhaps competitively since there are a lot) than Cafe Desta but the quality here I felt was very high, the food quite authentic, and the portions are not lacking. I wouldn't mind seeing a few more vegetarian dishes such as okra or sweet potato stews on the menu, but the essentials were here. However, I plan to return in particular for more of that -great-injera and to try the other vegetarian dishes such as the Gomen, Misir Alich'a and Fosolia, ------------ Okay here's a quick update to this review, went back for the lunch special today of three entrees of my choice, plus a side order of Ayeb (a dry cottage cheese that is a good counterpoint to spicy meats). This time I had the Kaye Asa (berbere Tilapia stew), the Fosolia and the Kik (yellow split peas). My favorites so far...the Tikil-Gomen (aka Ye'Atakilt Alich'a, sorry, I know it by another name!), the Kik and the Kaye Asa, in that order. But the Fosolia was good, just the other three are better! Oh, well of course the delicious Injera, which I needed to order an additional piece of! Another great meal, pleasant service and fresh food. And with a steamed milk, still barely $10., great deal for lunch.

text: Went to Buckets on the back of the 4 meals and 4 beers for $22 deal Groupon that was posted on Sunday. First off I'll list the good since most people don't read the entire review anyway! The projection screens are huge and you can watch sporting events from anywhere in the place. The images are clean and clear as well which is nice. GREAT JOB on installing them. The place is very large, much bigger than I had expected and it shouldn't be elbow to elbow even on busy nights or afternoons. Food: The food was your basic bar and grill fare as far as options go. My parents who tagged along as we needed four people to complete the groupon deal, enjoyed their Cheddar Burger (mother) and Shrimp Basket (father). They really piled on a ton of shrimp in the basket and the tails were already off which he enjoyed. I tried a few of them and they tasted like what you'd expect a fried shrimp to taste like. Speaking of the cheddar burger, which both my mother and i had, it was a healthy sized half pound patty that was nicely seasoned and very juicy. I was worried that the "cheddar" burger would actually just have a piece of american cheese on it but it did indeed actually have a piece of cheddar that you could taste the sharpness in. Very well done on your burger sir. My fiancee had the philly steak. Yes, I realize it's nearly impossible to replicate the philly you get up in PA but this wasn't offensive and was better than some of the other places you can get one. Nice size. You could also tell the fries were cooked in fresh oil. BEER: Nice selection of beers on tap. My gripe here is that there's no list offhand to look at, so unless you want to make your waitress recite the list over and over each time you consider a new beer, you're gonna have to get up and head to the bar to see what's on tap. As the groupon was for draft beers I didn't ask if they had a bottle selection or not so I can't speak on that end. They do have Jai Alai, Dogfish head, and Magic Hat on tap plus all the regular stuff and I'm sure a few others. SERVICE: The service kinda ebbed and flowed. There's no sign that says to seat yourself so we stood at the entrance for a few minutes and nobody acknowledged us so we went and grabbed a booth. We sat there for another 15 minutes before anyone stopped by to take our drink orders. Once that was done the service was very efficient (perhaps they just hadn't noticed us?) until the end of the meal. A gentleman, who I assume might be the owner, stopped by to ask us how everything was which is always a nice touch to see concern for a budding business. It did take awhile for us to get our bill though at the end, so like I said, the service kinda ebbed and flowed throughout the evening. FINAL THOUGHTS: All in all, we'll go back there as I'd like to try their wings as well and perhaps something else on the menu just to get a better feel for the food. I think they could make some refinements on the menu (such as listing the available toppings for burgers) and include some sort of beer list, even if it's only posted on a giant chalk board somewhere (if they have rotating taps). Prices were average and the beer was very cold and that was a good thing. I can't stress enough how nicely the viewing lines and screens are for viewing sports.

I explained to her that as someone with Celiac we understand the concerns, but to please bring it back with a disclaimer and let the consumer/customer decide if it's worth the risk!!!! He has ALOT of money and can't be sued over something like that". I explained to her that he wouldn't be sued. That places do this all the time, much bigger chains than Pancake Pantry and much smaller places as well. That with a disclaimer he is free of any and all lawsuits. I explained how hard it is to live with a gluten intolerance and how much disrespect I gained for them for taking it away from people. We go really late in the day so never wait in line. But what if we had been like most people and stood outside for an hour+ to come in and be told "hey you can't eat here anymore". Or even worse. What if it was a family day and one of their kids couldn't have gluten. They got in and were told "sorry your kid can't have pancakes". I was simply trying to explain to her that there really isn't a good excuse -- at all -- for them not serving them anymore. For whatever reason, she wanted to literally ARGUE about it. It was the strangest thing I've ever seen. I can't even count how many things are wrong with what she said/did. I waited and talked to a manager who seemed very "nervous" when we talked to him. Where is the andouille and okra? Second Course: Commander Palace style shrimp remoulade - There were two large shrimp (yes two !!!) on the plate with a nicely spiced remoulade sauce and garnish. Taste was good what there was of it. Shrimp cocktail usually comes with six shrimp. Do you think they could at least serve four shrimp? Third Course: Shrimp etouffee served over jambalaya and Cajun style roast pork shoulder with smoked bacon over mashed sweet potatoes - Once again, two large shrimp on about 1 cup of jambalaya. The jambalaya was flavorful but unremarkable. I make better jambalaya as does Zatarains. Next to the jambalaya was about 1 cup of mashed sweet potatoes with a small amount (maybe 1 oz.) of pulled pork shoulder strings. The sweet potatoes were excellent. Fourth Course: White Chocolate Bread Pudding with whiskey sauce - This desert is to die for. I can not say enough about how GOOD this was. Go to Daddy Mims just for this desert. Skip the rest of the Taste of New Orleans. Yum !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Beverage: Unsweetened Iced Tea - The tea was weak. The tea bag was waved across the water. Sweetening options limited to sugar and Equal. Luzerne Tea is available in this part of the country. Luzerne is a southern robust tea not like a woossie Tetley. The service was very good to excellent. On a Sunday evening there were four two-top tables (besides us) and a party of six table being served. Maybe the crowds are getting the feed bag on somewhere else before coming to get the bread pudding desert later. Rating (max 4 stars): Overall - 2 stars. Value - 0.5 star. Food - 1.5 stars. Service - 3 stars. Atmosphere - 2.5 stars. Finally, I will never pay $40.00 for the Tour of New Orleans again due mainly to the portion sizes. If it were not for the desert this meal would have been a total rip-off. Americans want a good meal, large belly busting portions and low low prices. We are NOT the French !!!!!!!!!!!!

text: I have been trying to find a solid "nice" pizza place in Philly for years; after my first trip to Rocchino's, I'm still searching. The decor was pleasant, if unremarkable, with the pizza oven serving as a focal point towards the back. The chairs were comfortable and, aside from a slight draft and strange lack of other customers, it was a nice place to be. A waitress gave us menus, took drink orders and explained how they do their food "tapas style" so things come out as they're ready. This was my first source of aggravation, as they are a pizza/Italian restaurant. The current restaurant trend of using "tapas style" as code for "we can't coordinate our kitchen well enough to serve your meals together" needs to stop. We ordered two pizzas, the margherita and the sausage/broccoli rabe, which were thankfully brought out at the same time. To open with the positive, I will say the crust on these pizzas was spot on - crispy, slightly chewy, with just a few charred spots from the oven. However, aside from the crust, both pizzas were disappointing. They were very bland and required generous applications of red pepper flakes, parmesan cheese and (a first for me with pizza) salt to taste like anything. Yes, my pizza with sausage needed more salt. The pizzas are ~12", and should be viewed as "personal sized". I had a few slices left from mine, while husband finished his. Nothing was openly bad about our experience and, had we not spent $90 on two pizzas and a few glasses of wine, they might have gotten 3 stars. If they stay in business for another few months, I will assume things may have improved and would consider trying them again. In the meantime, I will continue to enjoy NYPD Pizza take-out, and keep hoping that one day I might show up to Zavino when they have less than a 40 minute wait.

text: More like Mediocre Dog. First and foremost, let me say that the fact that I am not an animal person, let alone a dog person, has zero impact on this review. My boyfriend and I were seated in the corner of the wall during my first visit to Good Dog on a Monday evening. It was more crowded than we had expected, and the restaurant somehow made a two-seater out of an awkward space in corner. I faced a wall, and Zack faced me on a diagonal. The beer served to Zack was flat, but they gave him a new one, no problem. I ordered a veggie burger because other Yelpers said it was the best. Zack ordered the Good Dog Burger, which he enjoyed although the roquefort was a bit overpowering. Although I was impressed that the veggie burger was homemade, with rice and lentils and mushrooms and all that good stuff, it was mushy and tasted of nothing except cumin and my #1 Least Favorite Taste - 'effin cilantro. Once it's in your mouth you can't escape the flavor, am I right? The fries had great potential (a mix of sweet and regular) but were lukewarm and soggy, like they were from the bottom of the bag or were sitting in the warmer too long. Three days later I found myself at the Good Dog again to meet friends. There was a line, on a Wednesday at 7:30, and we were ushered to the third floor to wait for our names to be called. As soon as we got upstairs, I felt like I was in high school, sipping beer in someone's poorly-lit finished basement. Groups of people were sitting on the carpeted floor, or in chairs set up in a circle. Only this time, I was drinking some fancy IPA and not a Coors Light. We hunted down the hostess after about 20 minutes and she decided that yes, it was time for us to sit down. I got the beet and goat cheese salad, which did not taste fresh and light like a salad should. The goat cheese balls were breaded and deep fried. text: So... my wife and I were long awaiting the new arrival of a restaurant from the folks at Rasa Sayang. Man, were we gravely disappointed. I don't know if it's possible to put a finger on EXACTLY what was bad about this place, since it ended up that there are just multiple small things that added up and left bad tastes in both our mouths. First of all, Rasa Sayang it is not! Whereas Rasa Sayang has picked a quiet corner of Independence Mall and carved out a niche of Malaysian cuisine, Padi sits prominently in the center of Lantana Shopping Center boasting an eclectic menu of Thai, Malaysian, and Japanese! This restaurant takes a wrong turn on all three of those, leaving sub-par flavors that may unfairly keep you away from other Thai, Malaysian, or Japanese restaurants. Folks, this is a Chinese restaurant masquerading as pan-Asian cuisine and preying on unknowing patrons of the Hockessin community. The best way to describe the food is extremely bland and homogeneous. Thai food should be a bouquet of flavors, not just blends of soy sauce and sriracha. My wife ordered their drunken noodles (pad-kee mao) and an eggplant curry. The drunken noodles tasted like lo-mein with sriracha and a couple of basil leaves thrown on top for decoration, the eggplant curry looked and tasted exactly like the eggplant dish you can get at the Great Wall Chinese Restaurant in Pike Creek (and that is a take-out establishment). I ordered their "Hibachi Chicken," which I found to be lacking salt, pepper, ginger and garlic (the last time I was at a Hibachi restaurant, and the chef cooked the chicken in front of me, these were the four ingredients he used to make the hibachi chicken). In other words, the dish at Padi was just chicken prepared on a griddle, not necessarily the type of dish you get at a hibachi restaurant. I did not try the sushi, but with the three bombs they served up, I think I might just head over to Mikimoto's in Wilmington, if I get a hankering. The decor was faux-trendy, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but after having experienced the quality of the food, I find it hard to not think "lipstick on a pig."

How convenient. Complimentary Homemade Biscuits and Preserves- The most memorable biscuits ever! Warm, light, fluffy, and slightly buttery. They weren't extremely buttery or salty like some of the others I have had in the past. Three types of preserves come with your plate of biscuits: Peach, Blackberry, and Strawberry. The biscuits are delicious on their own but the preserves are so well made, you will want to buy a jar of it to take home. Two simple ingredients go into their preserves, sugar and fruit. Southern Sampler Breakfast - Includes Country Ham, Bacon, Sausage and Eggs. All Breakfast Platters come with your choice of grits or potatoes. The Ham was flavorful but really tough. You will be chewing for a very long time. The red eye gravy was flavorful. The bacon was savory, crispy, and slightly salty. The sausage patties were warm, tender, and seasoned well. The eggs were cooked perfectly, just the way I ordered them- sunny side up. The grits were warm and comforting but a bit too watery for me. French Toast- Hearty slices of Texas toast with loads of cinnamon and sugar. It comes with syrup, but they were delicious on their own. Hashbrown Casserole- Potatoes + Cheese = winner {Price Range} Breakfast Plates/Platters $6.95-$13.50, Supper Platters $9.95-$16.95 When thinking about the biscuits at Loveless Cafe, words such as "amazing" and "mind blowing" come to mind.

My only complaint, and this is legit as my partner and I spend a huge chunk of our money on sushi there, is that their happy hour sucks if you think it includes sushi. Each of the six pieces it was sliced into contained 1, maybe 2 tiny squares of dry chicken, only half of those had a single paper thin sliver of red onion, and so little cilantro, it had no business being on the menu. Even a picky pizza loving kid would be disappointed with this skimpy excuse for a flat bread. Anything pre-frozen from the grocery store would have had more flavor and toppings than this did. Two of the guys I went with ordered their wings. The original sauce tasted more like sweet and sour sauce from a Chinese restaurants and their hottest sauce is mild at best. These guys were not too satisfied. My other two friends ordered the spinach salad and it was piled high with an appetizing presentation. It had lots of chicken swirling on top and I was told it was dressed well. As far as traditional bar food is concerned, this place is a flop. text: My boyfriend & I are brand new to the South Side and we were cruising for some good 'ol westernized Chinese food. Famished, I looked up the closest Chinese Restaurant on my phone and up came Tin Tin. The place looked pretty sketchy but the parking lot was full so how bad could it be, really? We walked in and were surprised to find it packed full of Asian families. You never see that in a westernized Chinese food restaurant so we figured it was a traditional Dim Sum joint. We both don't have the stomach or pallet for Dim Sum but we were so hungry we sat down anyways. To our surprise they served both! They had a straight up Dim Sum menu written in Chinese - no English translation - and a separate English menu with items that were more to our liking. No whole duck for me, thanks! We ordered the dinner for two which consisted of 2 Spring Rolls, 2 Small Wonton Soups, Chicken Fried Rice and 2 items of your choice. We chose Szechuan Beef & Shanghai Noodles. The waiter wasn't very friendly when taking our order and when we inquired about swapping one wonton soup for a hot and sour soup (boyfriend is not fond of wonton), he shut us down immediately before I could even finish the question. I know it's kind of douchy to ask for different items on a set menu but c'mon, it's soup. A small, tiny, appetizer soup. But life goes on. Our main courses were brought out pretty fast considering the restaurant was packed full. The food was delivered by a much happier fellow whom we took for the night's supervisor (or something). It was your standard Chinese food; it tasted good but it was one of the greasiest Chinese food I've ever had. I had a hard time eating my noodles because they were so heavily doused in oil I couldn't get a grip on them with my chopsticks. It was rather embarrassing since I consider myself sort of a chopstick prodigy, you know, no big deal. I had to switch to a fork in shame. I think the whole thing came to $30 bucks. It wasn't awful or anything but I can think of a lot of places where $30 bucks gets you better food, better service and a better atmosphere.

text: This was the worst pizza I've had in Santa Barbara. Except for the fact that the restaurant was clean, every aspect of my experience was negative. The pizza is generally crappy. I bought two slices, adding sausage and olives to each. They charge fifty cents per topping per slice, and the slices are already nearly $4.50. Yes, the slices are large, but $5.50 for a slice of sausage & olive pizza is high. The sausage was low-grade and extremely thin-sliced, and looked and tasted like cardboard. The cheese, crust, and sauce were tasteless. In fact, the pizza itself tasted like cardboard. The Parmesan cheese sitting on the table was also tasteless. The red pepper in the shaker on the table was not spicy under any definition, and looked like the same flakes had been there since the Eisenhower years. In fact, the only thing that I could taste with dinner was grease, of which there was a great deal -- so much that it dripped off the pizza all over my hand and onto my plate. The cup of Coke was watery even when they brought it to me, and contained more ice than Coke. They also assess a surcharge for credit card transactions on any bill totaling less than twenty dollars. (Yes, that's right: TWENTY DOLLARS.) Total bill for two slices of tasteless pizza, a watered-down Coke, and a credit-card transaction? More than fourteen dollars. For low-grade dining, that's pretty expensive. I could have walked a block down the street and had a much more pleasant experience ordering a much better pizza and less watered-down Coke at the Santa Barbara Brewing Company for a dollar or two more, and it would have been far, far better. I could have had a far better pizza delivered to my house by Domino's (and I don't care much for Domino's) for two dollars more than they charged for a single slice, and that two dollars would be the delivery charge. I can't imagine why anyone would eat this pizza more than once. The music selection during the half-hour I was in the establishment consisted entirely of those 80s songs that have been forgotten for excellent reasons: Don Henley's less-inspired work (which is pretty bad, considering how good his better solo stuff was -- that is, not particularly good), Meat Loaf's most forgettable melodies (including "Two Out of Three Ain't Bad," which I've happily gone without thinking about for maybe six years now), and similarly charming selections. The lock on the (unisex) bathroom door was non-functional, but this was not apparent when I tried to lock it. (It turns, but doesn't latch; there is a conspicuous lack of signage indicating this problem.) I was standing at the urinal when some frat boy in a Halloween costume (a doctor's coat with "Seymour Bush, gynecologist" embroidered over the heart) walked in. The employees were incredibly rude. When I was coming out of the bathroom and trying to walk around the line of people waiting to order, one of them was coming the opposite direction and pushed me out of his way. The other employee called a number for someone waiting to pick up an order, and, three seconds later, while the people were pulling their tickets out of their pockets to look to see whose attention he was trying to get, he /barked/ the same number again, angrily, at maximum possible volume. Absolutely no redeeming qualities. The only thing that made me happy during my dinner was noticing on my way out that the tip jar was empty.

text: I've been thinking about hypnotherapy for a while because I want a "quick fix". I'm tired of going to numerous sessions with psychologists and talking about a bunch of stuff, starting from my early childhood and family, hoping that the root of my issues will slowly be found and resolved. Even though I've considered hypnotherapy as an alternative, I didn't do it sooner because: 1) I'm scared (I know hypnotherapy is a legit form of psychological therapy and all but I still can't help being spooked thanks to TV and movies) 2) The sessions are expensive But I finally became desperate enough to be willing to pay for a session. After all, if it really does work, then it's actually a small price to pay in exchange for the invaluable positive changes that I haven't been able to change by myself. But in a twist of fate, there was a hypnotherapy offer on Living Social the morning after! Out of all times! I've NEVER seen any of the coupon/deal websites offer hypnotherapy before, it was destiny! Before buying the Living Social deal, I did a little bit of research on his site to check everything out. According to his website, he also has an MA in psychology which made me feel better knowing that he has a legit degree to back him up and not just a "certificate"... no offense. I probably would not have found Greenwood Hypnotherapy without the Living Social deal as his main location is in Folsom and I would have only looked locally. He also has a location in Sacramento near Sac State in which he is there Tuesdays and Thursdays. I went to the Folsom location because it was the earliest appointment I could get and remember, I'm desperate! Mr. Greenwood was very helpful with me, answering my emails inquiring about setting an appointment and also messaged me on Facebook to notify that he had more appointments available. When I got there, he was very warm and friendly. I was very scared and he spent his time to explain the whole process with me in detail and did not rush anything at all, despite maybe having to take more time on my evaluation. He made an effort to make sure I was comfortable when I tried to relax and "fall asleep". Unfortunately, I was still freaked out and scared about the whole process so I wasn't able to use the in-person session to it's full advantage. I tried my hardest to relax but my body was tense. I was afraid I was going to be put in a trance and hallucinate LOL. At the end of the session, he said that if I had any questions or concerns to feel free to contact him. He recorded the session and gave me the CD to listen to at night. He also gave me a prerecorded optimism CD that I have yet to listen to. The interesting thing that I wasn't expecting is that every night I listen to my CD before going to sleep, I always have dreams. I am a very rare dreamer, with maybe only one every couple months that I can recall in the morning, and when I don't listen to the CD, I don't have dreams either. The only other thing that I have experience with that gave me "forced" dreams was this certain psychiatric medication. Hmm, it must be having some effect on the brain! I did hear some mouse click noises during my session along with the sound happening outside the office, which also recorded onto the CD. I suggest that he maybe consider one of those trackpads/touchpads, like the ones on laptops, where you can lightly tap to click and or a directional microphone instead of an omnidirectional one. Another thing I'd suggest is for the website to be cleaned up. As a former web design hobbyist, I think the colours are clashy, the pages look busy, and overall looks a bit "infomercially" and I don't think that's the vibe a therapy type business is going for. Speaking of the website, he does have a collection of prerecorded hypnosis mp3s available for sale. They are more generic and aren't made specifically for an individual, but they are more affordable. I don't want to publicly admit this, but the reason I went to see him was because I wanted to improve my study habits and I also have a tendency to skip lectures... a lot. Let me put this in perspective: I took three classes last quarter and for two of the classes, I showed up to the first midterm not knowing what the professor even looked like... Yeah. It's been about 4 weeks since my hypnotherapy session and I haven't been listening to my CD every single night, but this quarter I have not missed any classes and I am studying a little everyday (not as much as I should but it's been a big improvement compared to before which was basically not at all) I've been telling my friends about my whole hypnotherapy experience and some of them have similar problems as I do. They are keeping an eye on my progress because they are seriously considering hypnotherapy now too!
label: POS

text: Nu-Image has undoubtedly lost any sense of decency or quality it used to possess. What happened??? I called at 9am a couple of weeks ago to make an appointment for a manicure, pedicure and waxing. I wanted to come in at 11 and they insisted I come in at 10:30. I agreed thinking this was because they were busy. When I arrived I was the only person there. The pedicure was okay, but definitely rushed. I asked for shellac for my manicure as I had had it on already. Instead of soaking my nails to remove the old shellac, they filled it off with one of those tolls you'd use for acrylics. This made my nails thin, weak and brittle. They then went to put on the shellac, painting it so thick that it dried uneven and clumpy looking. I insisted that they take it off, as it looked horrible, and they used the electric nail file again to take it off! At this point I was not going to give them another chance so I ended up with no polish and weak nails. Mind you, through this entire nail fiasco the woman who was attempting to do my nails was very short with me and refused my requests. I then went to get waxed and it was as if I was placed in a storage closet with just a couple amateur waxing tools. The woman had absolutely no idea what she was doing, she was rough with me and it took her over an hour. The spa had become a little busier by now and her coworkers were annoyingly yelling at her through the door to hurry up and finish so she could go do nails. What kind of customer service is that??? Icing on the cake? They charged me for everything! I have been a patron there for years! $95 dollars later with an okay pedicure, unpainted weak nails and sore skin. HANDS DOWN THE WORST SPA EXPERIENCE EVER. I will never step foot in that place again. I advise you don't.. There are plenty of other affordable nail spas in town.

text: This place is awesome...like going back in time! When my wife and I were getting our bike trailer tuned up at Velo Champ, I noticed that a little bakery had popped up next door. Mikey's had a window-full of wedding cakes that looked like contenders for yet another Food Network reality show. But down in the corner sat a bottle of Cheerwine...and that is what made me stop and go inside. We had our 18 month old with us so once we were in the door there was no turning back. Mikey's is a charming bakery cafe with an elaborate display case and lots of antique accessories that were so appropriately well placed that I might have thought that we stepped back in time for a minute...back to a Seminole Heights soda fountain in the 30s or 40s. In actuality, I found out they just opened last Wednesday! Our son walked right up to the case and insisted that he must partake. Much to my pleasure, there was a semi-familiar sight. Many of the gourmet concoctions resembled French pastries. After living for a few months in the south of France, I grew an addiction to Pain au Chocolat. Sure enough there on the bottom rack my little son was pointing right at them. Well done my boy! Of course these did not feign to be authentic...just amazingly good as the ribbons hanging from the case attest to. There was a label announcing that they were chocolate croissants. And that they truly were. Unlike their French twins, they didn't leave anything to the imagination as they were oozing out the sides with chocolate. In fact, after ordering one (served warm) I determined that it was 50% chocolate at least. Yummy, and the flakiness/tender thickness of the rectangular croissant was almost right on. My wife and I determined it was time for lunch and promptly ordered their Southern Philly on Cuban Bread. And watch out Geno's...this cheesesteak was gooood! What makes it Southern I suppose is the thin spread of delicious peppercorn ranch dressing that compliments the juicy roast beef, green peppers, onion, and provolone melting in your mouth on that fresh soft cuban bread. Did I mention that they also had two shelves of pies (including a gooey pecan) which means I am going to have to bypass the chocolate croissant next time? When I return, I'll try one of their homemade soups too, like Tomato Basil or Chicken n'Dumplings. Their laid back and helpful staff were friendly and professional making me want to find another good excuse to return to the Seminole Heights neighborhood again soon.

text: Ended up making a day trip to Philadelphia, and one of the spots that I had to stop by for lunch was Village Whiskey. I've heard great things about this place, so I HAD to try it out and see for myself what all the buzz was about. This place is small but we didn't have any problem getting a table for 4 without having to wait. You can either sit inside, with a bar-styled seating, or go outside and enjoy the weather. Obviously we decided to sit outside because it was a perfect day. With Village Whiskey, you're either coming here to drink, or eat their burgers. For $11, you can get a solid Village Burger, that tastes amazing. I went the extra mile and added the truffled mushrooms for $5, which I so do not regret. The burger is huge. You literally might even get lock jaw trying to eat this bad boy. The bun comes nicely toasted, with a kind of thousand island spread to it. Your patty is like no regular patty. It's literally over an inch thick, and has a nice light char to it. Inside, you get a nice juicy patty which brings joy to your taste buds. On top of you burger, you have to have something else to snack on. The duck fat french fries ran $5 an order. Sure, it was pretty tasty, but I'm actually not sure what the buzz is with duck fat. It's not like it tasted any different from regular oil. Sure I ate every single one, but for $5, I had at least hoped for a larger portion. Either that, or my taste buds are seriously flawed. Village Whiskey is in an awesome location. Right in the heart of downtown Philadelphia, this place is a treat. I was lucky to have this for lunch on my first trip to this city, and if I come back, I'll make it a point to stop by and grab another burger.
label: POS

text: Tacos! First place I stopped by after landing in New Orleans. It was pouring and I was tired from my flight but my girlfriend pulled me along so we drove over and squished over in my flip flops and sat by the bar. I ordered the Mr Biggs plate which allows for a choice of 4 tacos, a side and a beef patty - I ordered a side of jerked veggies, duck taco, pulled pork, scallop and the chopped shrimp. My gf ordered the mahi mahi salad and despite he warning of about the large portion size i also ordered the guac and chips. The salad portions were really big, it was a mound of greens and grilled fish. The tacos were great, the duck was smoky, the pork was tender with alot of sauce and the scallop was fresh and not overly cooked. One thing i noticed was that they placed a leaf of lettuce as a base between the tortilla and the filling which kept the tortilla from getting soggy and falling apart. Tortilla while good, I'm not sure if it was the best I had, I'm not sure if its made in house but it didn't have that nutty roasted corn taste that I really like from some of the home made tortillas in the food trucks in NYC. But I must say surprisingly what left a really big impression on me was the beef patty... the crust was flaky, the filling was steaming and when you swallow, the tingling of Caribbean spices lingers on the back of your tongue. MAN it was good. The Guac and chips were really fresh, if you're from NYC i would say it was on par or better with the usual places like rosa mexicana etc. It was fresh, there was alot of it and it was cheap. The chips are made in house so it was salty with a all that oily goodness. After stuffing your face, you sit back, watch saints game in the background, a corona in your hand, the rain pattering in the background, its as good as it gets.
label: POS

text: I went to this museum after planning for 2 years. It was well worth it. The layout is 2 floors, an upper and lower gallery, most exhibits in old fashioned glassed in cabinets and smaller than you would think it to be. Still after spending 2 hours there I didn't see everything. When you go into this museum you will see many specimens that have been preserved in the old way: formaldehyde in glass jars. There is a wall of skulls named and catalogued as to how the individual died. There are shrunken heads and imitation shrunken heads. An abnormally large colon is displayed like a huge leather warped kiddie tunnel. You can find out many about other specimens online. There is so much to look at. The thing that really impressed me was the design of the museum and its exhibits. It looks very old (but if you find a picture of what it originally looked like you'd see it was much more crammed and less organized than today,) with polished wood and glass everywhere. If you didn't know better you'd think it was a classy freak show. It is not. It's associated with the The College of Physicians of Philadelphia. And that doesn't just mean that you get to see historic medical samples there are lectures on health (like pox,) and disorders (Like the elephant man John Merrick,) physical systems (childbirth,) and mental illness (the stalking of a high school teacher by a student.) They have special events like readings and receptions CSI style. If you enjoy gory subjects and physical deformities arouse your curiosity not your disgust, this place will make you very happy. If you're uncomfortable when you see someone's nose bleed or you get nauseous because there's a huge pimple on your friend's nose don't come here. The wax models leave little to imagination and the fetus will leave you with nightmares. Another thing; if you need slick exhibits to garner your interest or action to pique your curiosity this is not the museum for it. Every exhibit is static. If you like history though, go. Interested in physical disabilities, Abnormal tumors or mutations, go! I loved it and hope to go again! As far as children go, if the kids you are planning to bring are goosey, don't like macabre subjects or are prone to running around and screaming because they have no concentration skills don't bring them. It's sad to see parents bring kids that can't control themselves or are uncomfortable with the subject matter here. There really are no interactive exhibits or hands on displays for them.

text: Loved this place! Go here! Bizarre, kind of hidden away, with high-quality food and friendly service at fair prices. I was visiting family in Santa Barbara and had never heard of the Dutch Garden before. The beer selection is so, so fantastic if you like German beer (who doesn't?) and the food (I had bratwurst and sorrel soup) was also extremely good. The table ordered a sausage sampler, so I got to try most the others -- all of them were fantastic, especially the Polish. The ambiance is awesome and VERY relaxing in a quirky, homey way -- white and red checkered table cloths, randomly placed gnome figurines, and a super outdoorsy patio area (where we sat) that makes it feel almost like you're having a private party. Inside is a little bar that resembles a diner-style counter, which is charmingly funky and is where I would have wanted to sit had I been there with a party of just two or three. Off the bar is the grill area where the owner himself (who is the man, more on that later) cooks most if not all of the main courses. It feels kinda like a house converted into a restaurant (maybe it is?). The service, as others have mentioned, goes at what I'll call a casual pace -- not slow or inattentive, just not super-rushed like modern upscale restaurants just trying to turn over tables. (Our server and busser were both extremely attentive, bringing us multiple rounds of drinks, water, and other requests before and during the meal.) Anyway, you aren't doing this place right if you're trying to get in and out in 30 minutes. You really need to sit and enjoy the place for what it is. Preferably with multiple beers. Now, the following story is what tipped this place from a 4.5 to a 5.5 for me (yes, I would like to add another half star above the allowable amount). Dutch Garden happened to be serving what is probably my favorite Pilsner -- nay, beer, I will say -- brewed on this bright green globe, Pinkus. Usually, when a place carries this beer (which is almost never), I get overly excited about it and everyone looks at me funny. I love it. And guess what? Dutch Garden not only had it, BUT THEY SERVED IT IN A CUSTOM PINKUS GLASS! Hot balls! I had never seen the custom glass before, so at this point I was ridiculously happy. I was incredulous such a thing could exist to complement such an already awesome other thing. Could I buy one of these?, I asked our server. You can ask that guy right inside there, she said, he's the owner. So mid-meal, I get up, walk inside, and proceed to ask as nicely and humbly as I can whether there is any chance of this happening. I think I offered him $10, $15 bucks at one point. This guy hears me. He WANTS to sell me one. But, alas, they only have a handful and he knows as well as I that a beer goes best in its properly designed glass (with tiny little cartoon brewer dudes on it, so rad). Anyway, he's sorry. Can't do it. It's cool, I say. This was hardly an everyday request, after all. An hour later, as we're walking out, he yells at my brother: Hey, get that guy! I am summoned over to his grilling station, where, to my surprise, he hands me one of the very same Pinkus glasses in a rolled-up paper bag. No problem, he says, he put in a call to his distributor and they're gonna send him a few more. No need to pay for it. It's on the house. I think I high-fived him. I really don't remember the details. The way I acted, this guy probably thought he was going to have to scrape my brains off the wall of his restaurant. But he acted cool about it, like it was no problem. This was really the icing on the cake of an already stellar night out to dinner, so for that, owner of the Dutch Garden, I salute you. (And I apologize in advance if people come in there trying to buy beer glasses from you now. But it was probably the best part of the experience, which was all-around awesome. Thanks again!)

text: This is a somewhat hard review to write as the food was actually fairly good, but the service was so terrible, that I can't go higher than two stars. We arrived at 6:15 and were promptly seated, that is unfortunately where the positives of the night ended. Shortly before our drinks arrived another waitress stopped by and asked us if we had been helped yet. I so wanted to blurt out "yes but our waitress is MIA", but alas I did not. Probably should have as she seemed a much more attentive waitress. It was 6:40 before we received our drinks and after 7:00 when we received the first two things we ordered. Our waitress apologized at least four times (probably the number of times she visited our table) for things being slow. She commented they are not usually so busy on a Sunday night. After hearing that I looked around and they were probably less than 50% full, but the kicker here was the Cards were playing in the World Series this night, why would you not expect a few more people than normal? All in all it took us an hour and a half to have a drink, and eat three items, which in my opinion was about 45 minutes more than it should have taken. Ok, now I can move onto the actual food. We ordered the grilled cheese which supposedly came on sourdough with a blend of cheeses. On the happy hour menu this is a steal at $3. My better half will argue that the sourdough is not real sourdough, but that is her battle not mine. The grilled cheese was pretty good and came with a plate of french fries. Next we ordered the buffalo chicken flat bread. It was ok, the buffalo sauce was good, had a nice flavor and was not spicy for the sake of being spicy. The last thing we got was the Ice Kitchen Wings. Again, the buffalo sauce was good and had a subtle heat to it. You didn't notice it till about the fourth or fifth wing, but it was there. Not hot, just enough to let you know it was there. If I was just rating them on their food, I would rate them a solid 3.5, but the overall experience was just Meh. The manager was more concerned with turning on the sound for the Cards game than dealing with a table that flat out sent everything they ordered back. Unless you like within walking distance I would not recommend this place. I don't say that often and combine that with the fact it's way out of our way, I can safely say we will never be back.

text: There's only one thing I get when I go to Cicero's without fail: Trisha's wrap. I haven't been when there's a live band or for the beer or pizza, but I love the wraps. And I love sitting outside on Delmar while eating one. Cicero's is a cool restaurant, because it has a great location in the Delmar Loop in University City. It occupies one corner where the Loop begins near the stone lions just a little ways away, and commonly features local bands from around the area playing live music on weekends. Most of this is a moot point for me though. I come to Cicero's in the spring and summer (before it gets too hot to sit outside) for lunch or dinner and each time I get the same thing. Trisha's wrap is perfect because it's a combination of grilled chicken, spinach, mushrooms and Provel cheese all grilled up and melted together inside of a perfectly pressed wrap. It's ooey, gooey, drippy and delicious! Nothing nutritionally sound, I know (especially when paired with their french fries or, even better, onion rings) but so, SO good. Sure, Cicero's has plenty of other good fare: fresh made pizzas, sandwiches, pasta, salads, burgers (one is the Lions Gate Burger, which is a full pound of meat!) and seafood, etc. Basically something for everyone, but my go to is the wrap. And trust me, sitting outside in the shade people watching, enjoying a beverage and noshing a tasty lunch on the weekend is great. I love people watching in general, and the Loop has some of the most interesting characters on foot and some showing off their rides as they cruise slowly up and down Delmar. Believe me, if you want to see things you won't see anywhere else in St. Louis, the Loop is the place to be.

text: We've been here twice and have had a blast each time. It's approachable Italian food and honestly, reminds me some of the best meals I had when I was living in Italy. Between the food and the service, I really can't say enough good things. The key is to go with a group of people who don't mind sharing. It's worth trying as many dishes as you can. The bread that comes out is supposedly focaccia, but it's richer and more buttery than any other focaccia I've tasted. For five people, we got the braised snails, bufala ricotta crostini, a mixed salumi plate, and arancini to start. The arancini normally only comes with 4 portions, but they kindly added on a fifth for us. The snails were tasty and not too chewy; and the ricotta was creamy, but I wish it would have had more of the tang that I associate with ricotta di bufala. That didn't stop me from asking for more bread to finish it off though. I'm never one to order mixed salumi by myself, but let's just say that my sister, who rarely eats meat, set up camp at the pork terrine. And the arancini are little pops of goodness with their creamy, savory interior and crispy exterior. For our entrees, we decided to tackle the pasta section since it all looked so good and seemed to take advantage of spring's bounty. We ordered the tonnarelli "cacio e pepe," the bucatini ai fagioli, the fettucine with lamb ragu and mint, the chard ravioli, and the wilted spinach as a side dish. And they brought us a dish of their special pasta that night- a sweet pea agnolotti- "on the house." It's so hard to pick a favorite pasta here, and in fact, when we all went around to name our favorite, we each picked a different one! I loved all of them as the pasta was perfectly cooked and the sauces clung to each of them beautifully. But if i could only eat one dish again, I would go for the fettucine with the lamb ragu and mint. Now I'm normally not a lamb fan, but the tiny shreds of gamy lamb worked so well with the brightness of the mint. The sauce had body that helped it cling to each noodle, but it didn't overpower the flavor of the pasta. If you're going for the first time, definitely order the tonnarelli in your mix. It's a super-luscious version of the butter, noodles, and cheese dish you used to make 9or still make) for yourself in college. And even though we were all full, we all wanted a little something sweet to round out the meal. Their dessert menu was well-thought; each of their desserts brought a little something different depending on what you were craving- sweet, doughy, cheesy, icy, fruity, crunchy, chocolatey, and nutty. We settled on the ricotta crumble tart, the polenta shortcake with strawberries and (killer) salted butter semifreddo, the Belgian style waffles, the special tiramisu, and the prosecco rhubarb granita. I'm usually a chocolate or nut fanatic, but my favorite of the bunch was the polenta shortcake. It wasn't overly sweet, and the corn/ strawberry combo with buttery ice cream was satisfying without being too rich. My second choice would be for the Belgian waffle because it's just so fun to eat, but the other desserts are not far behind. For five people with all of this food and two carafes of house wine, it was about 50pp. And we got a lot of food. This is definitely one of my favorite places in Philly, so I'm sad to hear that other people didn't have great experiences. I know I'll be back though!

He answered all of our "hey, what's that?" questions. I don't usually go into lots of details on specific food items because my tastes are my tastes, but we hit high point after high point and I enjoy running through the night's menu in my head: the roast oysters were the spiciest (yay) Cajun food I had the entire trip, and the fried alligator was new to me and a real treat. For entrees we had the red fish which was not over-produced for a blackened fish, and the highlight was the Louisiana cochon with cabbage. We loved the mac and cheese too (though we did not need more food at that point), and our unofficial waiter brought us a small place of head cheese with mustard and pickles as guests of the kitchen. This is definitely a place we will always return to, a fantastic night. $120 for dinner or two, two drinks each.

The bread was rather sweet which makes sense considering Viitals is a bakery. The Unexpected wasn't quite filling enough for me to call lunch over, so I went back for round two. Next up, was a coconut-poppy seed macaroon. I'm not one to count calories, but I always like to know what's in my food. One great thing about Viitals is that the nutrition information is listed for all of their items. So for 160 calories, 5 g of protein and 5 g of fiber, this little treat hit the spot. text: (I started this review on my iPhone in October 2010 but only now am just posting it) Given the explosion of self-serve frozen yogurt joints on the Main Line in the past year, I had to try the newest addition to see how it compared to Yapple Yogurt in Wynnewood and Kiwi Yogurt in Haverford. I stopped on my way home from center city and found the place empty (not surprising at 4pm) except for someone chatting it up with the girl behind the counter. Top This is exactly like its competitors in that you take an oversized cup, fill it with any flavor(s) of the cold soft stuff, add toppings then weigh to pay. All 3 places charge $0.49 per ounce so if you're not careful you can easily create a $5 dessert. None of the fro-yo places provide a scale for you to see how much dessert you've accumulated before the check out counter. They should. But I know why they don't. Whereas Yapple Yogurt and Kiwi are bright, shiny and clean places with attentive employees that are constantly wiping off the toppings bar of stray chocolate chips or blueberries, Top This is depressing. Even though there were no customers in the store and it was clearly downtime, the toppings bar was a mess. The labels were falling off in some areas and the floor around the bar hadn't been swept; crumbs were just strewn on the dark floor. The checkout counter was piled with textbooks and other personal items, apparently because the employee happens to also be the co-owner and she's in grad school. I understand her need to study, but using your checkout counter as a desk? Really? The small counter against the wall behind the checkout counter was also cluttered with stuff. It was clear the owner wasn't serious about being a business. When I asked her how business was doing she admitted it was slower than she and the co-owner expected. I think she thought this fro-yo resurgence would make her and her partner easy money; people would flock to them because, why not, everyone loves fro-yo, and she's a local!! (She was a school teacher who grew up in the neighborhood). But, people also love a clean, well-kept business that is serious about serving, and keeping, customers. Her store should be pristine. She needs to keep her textbooks and personal effects off her counters, assiduously clean up the toppings bar and floor and simply make her investment a priority. Maybe since I was here in October it's improved. It can only go up from where it was (or it could just close its doors, which may be easier).

text: My Zake's experience was disappointing at best. We went early Saturday morning as we had some business in the area. Based on the average 4.5 out of 5 rating, and the anecdotal reports, I expected a great meal. We arrived 5 minutes before opening time so we waited a bit in the car so as not to impose. Others have commented on the lack of parking. When we arrived several cars were already parked in the lot but we were the only diners when we walked in at 8:05. The hostess/waitress seemed hurried as she seated us - mind you that we are the only diners. A young man (teenager dressed in a t-shirt and cargo shorts) asked in a hardly audible voice if we wanted anything to drink. Unfortunately, the expression on his face said, "Why do I have to be up this early on a Saturday morning?" We were brought our coffee. The waitress then took our order and we waited for 20 minutes or so for the order to come out. We are still the only customers in the place except for someone who came in for muffins to take out. When our food came out, both breakfasts were room temperature. The eggs were poached perfectly and sitting on a cold piece of red pepper on what was purportedly homemade French bread with an interesting tomato based sauce. I probably would have enjoyed the eggs had they been warm. They were served with the home fries which were not fried at all (more like steamed) and had no seasoning whatsoever except for some paprika for color. We ordered a side of bacon which appeared reheated from the day before. It was dried out and the color of chestnuts shells. The other entree we ordered was the lemon pancakes which were served with raspberries and caramel sauce. These were good (tasty but not the fluffy type) but undersized for the price we paid. (When you look at the pictures, compare them to the size of the cup holding the caramel sauce.) We were offered more coffee by the shorts-clad boy who proceeded to pour the coffee in both our cups by leaning the coffee pot against the lips of both of our cups. This was off-putting at best. Needless to say, at this point, 8:45, I was glad to see that we were still the only folks in the place. No one asked us how our meal was - they either already knew or didn't care to know. After that several groups of diners came in escorted by the waitress/hostess and assisted by the sullen boy and an additional young man with a pony tail who was equally uninspired. We finished our meal and declined another refill of coffee for obvious reasons. Finally, the waitress brought us our check. When we asked the sullen boy if we pay at the table or the bakery counter, he did not know and never did get us an answer as we never saw him again. After I took my cash from my purse, I looked up and for the first time, someone working there actually smiled - the second young man- who quickly swooped in, picked up the cash, and asked if we needed change. So if you don't mind poor service, ok but cold food, in a place whose charm has faded some and could use a good cleaning (including the restroom), try Zake's.

I arrive and, from the exterior, this place looks pretty legit. The name, "Beauty on Broadway" should have been a dead giveaway for the elevated tacky factor I would find inside...but as usual I was overly optimistic. In describing this place, I'm brought back to my roots, growing up in middle of nowhere East Texas. My aunt had a "beauty shop" where all of the elderly women would go for their perms and dye jobs. Quaint but far from classy or even "nice" for that matter. No real theme or even a stitch of modern decor. The decorative resemblance of BoB and my aunt's beauty shop was uncanny. Tabitha's Salon Takeover would have a hay day in this place....I still had hope though. Sometimes great things come in wal mart bag packages. I immediately cringe when I see THE stylist that will be doing my hair. And yes, THE means that there is only ONE. This Salon has only one person that does hair. I assumed this meant that she's perfect at her job and never requires a second opinion. (Why am I so optimistic?) During my consultation, I have photos with me of what I want and what I don't want....the "what I DON'T" photos literally look like just like the chick that's about to do my hair. Thick platinum streaks of blonde against differing dark shades of brown. Very 2000. I had these photos, because the last time I had my hair highlighted (years ago) the stylist did this to me...and I've lived in fear of highlights ever since....I wanted thin natural warm highlights. Simple. Nothing crazy. I felt it would be insulting to show her these photos of how much I hated her hair, so I just showed her the ones I liked... The process started and I was feeling very "qeu sera sera" about it all. She did my highlights, we had some "meh" small talk and then it was time to wash my hair.... fyi...THIS IS WHERE I STARTED TO GET ANNOYED First of all, the water was cold...the entire time. The sink was grimey and definitely needed a good scrubbing. She rinsed the highlights and then, on my wet hair, in the sink, applied the toner. She had me lay my head back on the hard sink for 15 minutes while the toner set. My head was freezing from the cold water, the back of my head was aching from resting on the porcelain sink, and I was bored out of my mind wondering when I was going to be rescued from this weird situation. Finally after she was finished texting on her phone, she comes to rinse out the toner. (Once again with cold water). She uses shampoo and conditioner but there was a distinct absence of the $25 "Conditioning Treatment" I was supposed to receive. I later ask her about this and she said she applied a mask to my hair when she was washing it....it was literally on my hair for maybe 15 seconds....Pshhh... She finishes my amazing hair salon experience with a quick trim of my hair (I asked for her to shape up my layers and bangs and she told me they didn't need it), she almost blow dries my hair to an actual dry state, and then sends me on my way....but of course asked for a tip before I left. Whew.... Take what you will from this and good luck. :)

The only downside I can think of about this place is that their actual address is a little screwy - you're officially supposed to have things shipped to 1229-1231 Chestnut St. PMB ###, and I've found that some online stores do address autocorrection and won't accept that address format. There is a ton going on at this time of year because of all the damage caused during the winter so that might have been an issue for some - We didn't have to pick anybody else up anywhere I'd say just allow for plenty of time if you're using this company in the Winter and you'll probably be fine.

text: For us, this was a rare lunch break since we usually work through them, but we ended early that day and decided to treat ourselves for a day well done. We arrived a little after the main lunch crowd had left but before the dinner crowd would be arriving so the place was relatively quiet with the exception of a few early birds.
